צא.def:
H3318. yatsa

יָצָא‎1068 verb go or come out (Late Hebrew id.; Aramaic יְעָא‎; Ethiopic , Assyrian âƒû DlHWB 237, all = go out, forth; Syriac go forth (in sense of germinate), grow; Phoenician יצא‎ march out; compare SI5 המוצא‎ the source (of water); Sabean וצַא‎ go out, DHM in MV; Arabic is be or become fair, beautiful, neat, clean, compare NöZMG 1886, 725) — Perfect יָצָא‎ Gen 10:11 92t.; 3 feminine singular יָָֽצְאָה‎ Num 16:35 13t.; יָצָ֑אָה‎ Isa 28:29; 2masculine singular יָצָאתָ‎ Gen 24:5 7t.; 2 feminine singular וְיָצָאת‎ Jer 31:4; 2masculine plural יְצָאתֶם‎ Exod 13:3; Deut 11:10 וִיצָאתֶם‎ Judg 21:21; Malachi 3:20; 3plural suffix יְצָאֻנִי‎ Jer 10:20, etc.; Imperfect יֵצֵא‎ Gen 15:4 64t.; וַיֵּצֵא‎ 4:16 132t.; 3 feminine singular תֵּצֵא‎ Exod 21:7 22t.; וַתֵּצֵא‎ Gen 30:16 14t.; 2 masculine singular תֵּצֵא‎ Deut 20:1 16t.; 3 plural יֵצְאוּ‎ Gen 15:14 +; יֵצֵ֑אוּ‎ 17:6 +; 3 feminine plural וַתֵּצֶ֫אנָה‎ 1Sam 18:6; 2Kin 2:24; וַתֵּצֶאןָ‎ Exod 15:20; 2feminine plural תֵּצֶ֫אנָה‎ Amos 4:3, etc.; Imperative צֵא‎ Gen 8:16 15t.; וָצֵ֑אָה‎ Judg 9:29; feminine singular צְאִי‎ Song 1:8; masculine plural Gen 19:14 11t.; צֵ֑אוּ‎ Isa 49:9; Ezek 9:7 + Jer 58:8 Qr (Kt יֵצֵ֑אוּ‎) צְאֶינָה‎ Song 3:11; Infinitive absolute יָצוֺא‎ Gen 8:7 2t.; יָצאֹ‎ 27:30 3t.; Infinitive construct צֵאת‎ 24:11 31t.; suffix צֵאתִי‎ Exod 9:29 3t.; צֵאתֵנוּ‎ Josh 9:12; צֵאתְךָ‎ Deut 16:3 10t., etc.; Participle יֹצֵא (יוֺצֵא)‎ Gen 2:10 62t.; feminine singular שֶׁיֹּצָא‎ Eccl 10:5; יֹצֵאת׳(יו )‎ Gen 24:15 11t.; יֹצֵת‎ Deut 28:37, etc.; —

1 go or come out or forth:

a. from (מִן‎) a place, e.g. a tent Gen 31:33 (E; opposed to בְ בּוֺא‎), מוֺעֵד אֹהֶל מִמֶּתַח‎ Lev 8:33; 10:7 (P), compare מִןהַֿמִּקְדָּשׁ‎ 21:22 (H); from a house 2Sam 11:8, the doors (דלתי‎) of a house Josh 2:19 (JE), Judg 11:31; ביתו מִפֶתח‎ Exod 12:22 (JE), from a camp 1Sam 13:17; 2Kin 7:12, a city Gen 19:14 (J), 12:4 (P), 1Kin 11:29; 20:17; Micah 4:10, a cave 1Sam 24:9, the ark Gen 9:18 (J), 8:16, 19 (both P); out of vineyards Judg 21:21; followed by accusative אֶתהָֿעִיר‎ Gen 44:4 (E), Exod 9:29 (J); with בְּ‎ also, of gate Jer 17:19; Neh 2:13; followed by accusative local. פָ֑תַח אֵצֵא לֹא‎ Job 31:34; participle construct הֵַתּבָה יֹצְאֵי‎ Gen 9:10 (P), עִירוֺ שַׁעַר יֹצְאֵי‎ 34:24 (P); absolute Josh 2:5 (JE), Judg 3:24; Exod 34:34 (P), Num 33:3 (P; Israel going out [from Egypt]), 2 h 26:20 +; specify., of going out (מִן‎) from a land (of emigration) Gen 10:11, 14; 24:5 (all J); patric. of coming forth from (the land of) Egypt (the Exodus) Exod 12:41 (J), 13:3, 8; 23:15; 34:18; Num 11:20; 22:5 (all J E), and especially D, Deut 4:45-46, 9:7; 11:10; 16:3 (twice in verse); 16:6; 23:5; 24:9; 25:17; Josh 2:10; 5:4-5, 6 (all D), Num 33:1 (P), 1Kin 6:1; 8:9 2Chr 5:10; 2Kin 21:15; Jer 7:25; Hag 2:5; Psa 114:1.

b go forth from (the presence of) a person: Exod 8:26; 9:33; 10:6 (all followed by מֵעִם‎), Gen 44:28; Exod 5:20; Jer 2:37 (מֵאֵת‎), Judg 3:19 (מֵעָלָיו‎); followed by מִלִּפְנֵי‎ Gen 4:16 (J), 41:46; 47:10; Est 8:15; Eccl 10:5; followed by מְּנֵי מֵעִם‎ Job 1:12, מְּנֵי מֵאֵת‎ 2:7; followed by suffix יְצָאֻנִי‎ Jer 10:20 (see De Eccl 7:18).

c. in technical senses: absolute go forth, of emancipation Exod 21:2-3,(twice in verse); 21:4-5, 7 (3 t. in verse); 21:11 (all J E), compare יַדאֲֿרָם מִתַּחַת יצא‎ 2Kin 13:5; of release in the year of jubilee, land, etc. Lev 25:28, 30, 31, 33 (all H), 27:21 (P); also of a debtor-slave 25:54 (H); suffix divorce מִבֵּיתוֺ וְיָָֽצְאָה‎ Deut 24:2; of condemnation רָשָׁע יֵצֵא בְּהִשָּֽׁפְטוֺ‎ Psa 109:7 when he is judged let him go out as a criminal, i.e. be condemned: of bowels (מֵעִים‎) falling out by reason of disease 2Chr 21:15, 19.

d. of flight, involving escape: followed by הַחוּ֫צָה‎, || נוּס‎, flee Gen 39:12, 15 (J), תֵצֵא נָצאֹ כִּי‎ Jer 48:9; opposed to taken (by lot) 1Sam 14:41; מִמֶּ֑נָּה לָצֵאת לֹאיֿוּכְלוּ אֲשֶׁר רָעָה‎ Jer 11:11 calamity from which they shall not be able to escape; perhaps also אֶתכֻּֿלָּם יֵצֵא אֱלֹהִים יְרֵא‎ Eccl 7:18 he that feareth God shall escape (or be freed from, see De Hi-Now Mishna) all of them (see VB), — on accusative with יצא‎ see De.

e. depart נַפְשָׁהּ בְּצֵאת‎ Gen 35:18 i.e. when she was expiring; so רוּחוֺ תֵּצֵא‎ Psa 146:4; מִנָּבָל הַיַּיִן בְּצֵאת‎ 1Sam 25:27 i.e. when Nabal became sober; also figurative לִבָּם וַיֵּצֵא‎ Gen 42:28 (E) i.e. their heart failed (|| וַיֶּחֶרְדוּ‎); rust from (מִן‎) caldron Ezek 24:16 (see Co 12:5); of glory of ׳י‎ 10:18; כָּלהֲֿדָרָהּ בַּתצִֿיּוֺן מִן וַיֵּצֵא‎ Lam 1:6; hence infinitive = exit, end הַשָּׁנָה בְּצֵאת‎ Exod 23:16 (JE), and, refundantly, שְׁנַיִם לְיָמִים הַקֵּץ צֵאת כְּעֵת‎2Chr 21:19 i.e. at the end of two years

f. of inanimate things: river out of Eden Gen 2:10 (J), water out of rock Exod 17:6 (E), Num 20:11 (JE), from Lehi Judg 15:19; of molten calf out of fire Exod 32:24(E); of gold (after refining) Job 23:10 (absolute, in simile); in prophecy of fountain from house of ׳י‎ Ezek 47:1, 8, 12; Zech 14:8; Joel 4:18; of seed (semen virile) from man Lev 15:16, 32 (P), 22:4 (H); of weapon which has pierced body 2Sam 2:23 (מֵאַחֲרָיו‎), 2Kin 9:24 (מִלִּבּוֺ‎), Job 20:25 (מִגֵּוַה‎); הַמֶּלֶךְ מַשְׂאַת אַחֲרָיו וַתֵּצֵא‎ 2Sam 11:8 and there went out ( = was sent out) after him the king's portion (i.e. the food given by the king); idiomatically of expenditure of money 2Kin 12:13 (absolute, compare Hiph`il v.12:12); of swift movement of arrow from bow Zech 9:14 (like lightning), of lightning out of fire Ezek 1:13; absolute of sunrise (subject שֶׁמֶשׁ‎) Judg 5:31 (in simile), Gen 19:23, compare Isa 13:10 (so Assyrian, e.g. ultu ƒît šanši adi êrib šanši COT Gen 19:23); of rising of stars (כּוֺכָבִים‎) Neh 4:15; of sentence of judge Hab 1:4 (twice in verse); Psa 17:2; of judgment, or right appearing (with simile of light) Hosea 6:5 (read יֵצֵא כָאוֺר וּמִשְׁמָּטִי‎), Isa 62:1; of a lot יוֺסֵף לִבְנֵי הַנּוֺרָל וַיֵּצֵא‎ Josh 16:1 (JE), and especially P, Num 33:54; Josh 19:1, 17, 24, 32, 40; 21:4, compare also גּוֺרָלָם גְּבוּל ויצא‎ 18:11 (P)

g. with especial emphasis on idea of origin, source: hyssop out of the wall 1Kin 5:13; הדבר יצא מיהוה‎ Gen 24:50 (J) from ׳י‎ has the thing proceeded, of a providential arrangement, so י ׳מֵעִם‎ Isa 28:29; רֶשַׁע יֵצֵא מֵרְשָׁעִים‎ 1Sam 24:14 (an ancient proverb); of pollution proceeding from (מֵאֵת‎) prophets Jer 23:15; of fire from Heshbon Num 21:28 (JE), Jer 48:45, compare Judg 9:15, 20 (twice in verse); of fire י ׳מִלִּפְנֵי‎ Lev 9:24; 10:2, י ׳מֵאֵת‎ Num 16:35 (all P); in theophany לְרַגְליו רֶשֶׁף יצא‎ Hab 3:5; iniquity from unreceptive heart Psa 73:7 (see I. הֵלֶב‎

1); wrath י ׳מִלִּפְנֵי‎ Num 17:11 (P); absolute Jer 4:4 = 21:12; 23:19 = 30:23; so salvation Isa 51:5; מִמֶּךָּ יָָֽצְאָה וְנִשְׁמַתמִֿי‎ Job 26:4; of words going forth from mouth of speaker (of solemn or formal speech) יֵצֵא לֹא דָּבָר מִמִּיכֶם‎ Josh 6:10 (JE), Judg 11:26; 1Sam 2:3; Jer 44:17; Job 37:2; Est 7:8, also Num 30:3; 32:24 (both P); of ׳י‎s words going forth from his mouth, or from him Isa 45:23; 48:3; 51:4; 55:11; Ezek 33:30; of ׳י‎s words, instruction, command, etc., going froth Isa 2:3 = Micah 4:2 (from Jerusalem), Dan 9:23; of human commandment Est 1:19, compare 1:17.

h. of children as going forth from loins (of father) מִמֵּעִים‎ 2Sam 7:12; 16:11; מֵחֲלָצִים‎ Gen 35:11 (P), 1Kin 8:19 2Chr 6:9; followed by מִן‎ alone 2Kin 20:18 = Isa 39:7; also יְרֵכוֺ יֹצְאֵי‎ Judg 8:30; Gen 46:26; Exod 1:5 (both P); also of birth מֵרֶחֶם‎ (אִמּוֺ‎) Num 12:12 (JE), Jer 1:5; 20:18; Job 3:11; figurative of sea 38:9; of ice 38:29; אִמּוֺ מִבֶּטֶן‎ 1:21; Eccl 5:14; literal, source not expressed, Gen 25:25-26, 38:28-29, 30 (all J); of untimely birth Exod 21:22 (JE); compare רַגְלֶיהָ מִבֵּין היּוֺצֵ֯ת‎ Deut 28:57 (|| תֵּלֵד‎); of family or race connection (followed by מִן‎) Nahum 1:11; Isa 48:1; 1Chr 1:12; 2:53; יצא‎ also of produce of vine (מִגֶּפֶן‎) Judg 13:14, compare הַשָּׂדֶה הַיֹּצֵא‎ Deut 14:22 (read ⅏ יצא‎, see Di); לֶחֶם יצא מִמֶּנָּה אֶרֶץ‎ Job 28:5; of viper proceeding from serpent's root Isa 14:29; further, with idea of unfolding, growth Job 8:16; 14:2; 31:40; יִשָׁ֑י מִגֶּזַע חֹטֶר וְיָצָא‎ Isa 11:1; of the little horn Dan 8:9; so of branches of candlestick in tabernacle Exod 25:32-33, 35; 37:18-19, 21 (all P); then simply project (tower from wall) Neh 3:25-26, 27; of measuring-line going forth (absolute) in a particular direction Jer 31:39; of a boundary (-line) going out (absolute) so as then to turn and make an angle Num 34:4, 9; Josh 15:3-4, 9, 11 (twice in verse); 16:2, 6, 7; 18:15 (twice in verse); 18:17 (twice in verse); 19:12-13, 27, 34, 47.

2. a. go forth to a place Gen 27:3 (J), Jer 14:18; Ezek 3:22; Zech 6:6 (twice in verse); 6:7 +; so הַמַּרְשְׁדֹ֫נָה וַיֵּצֵא‎ Judg 3:22 (see VB); go forth in surrender 1Sam 11:3 (followed by אֶל‎ person) 2Kin 18:31 = Isa 36:16; Jer 38:17, 21; יוֺצֵאת וְאֵין מֶּרֶץ אֵין‎ Psa 144:14; into captivity בַּגּוֺלָה אִתְּכֶם יָָֽצְאוּ לֹא‎ Jer 29:16, compare 48:7; Zech 14:2; also הַזֶּה מִןהַֿמָּקוֺם יָצָא‎ Jer 22:11, compare יְצָאֻנִי בָּנַי‎ 10:20.

b. go forward proceed to or toward something, figurative, יָצָ֑אוּ רָעָה אֶלֿ מֵרָעָה‎ Jer 9:2 from evil to evil they go on; in like manner 2Sam 20:8 si vera lectio, but read rather יָָֽצְאָה וְהִיא‎ and it (i.e. the sword) came out (of the sheath) and fell ᵐ5‎ We Dr Kit Bu.

c. come or go forth, with especially reference to purpose or result: וְהִכִּתִיו אַחֲרָיו וְיָצָאתִי‎ 1Sam 17:35, compare 24:15; נַפְשׁוֺ לְבַקֵּשׁ שָׁאוּל יָצָא‎ 23:15, compare 26:20, further 2Sam 2:13; 18:4; 1Kin 20:18 (twice in verse); 20:19, 39; 2Kin 5:2; Micah 1:11; Jer 37:5; Zech 14:3; Dan 11:11, 44 +; of an adulteress Prov 7:15; of an angel Num 22:32 (JE), Dan 9:22; for אִתְּכֶם ֗֗֗ יֵצֵא‎ 1Sam 22:3 (let my father etc.go forth [to be] with you, compare Klo) read perhaps יֵשְׁבוּ‎ as ᵑ9 ᵑ6‎ Kit, see also Dr; of army marching out to form battle line אֶלהַֿמַּעֲרָכָה יֹצֵא‎ 17:20 (with article, ᵑ0‎, < omitted by We Dr Kit Bu); יָָֽצְאוּ אֲשֶׁר בְּכֹל‎ Judg 2:15 in all to which they went forth, לפני יָצָא‎ 1Sam 8:20 of king going out at the head of his soldiers; so of ׳י‎ before his people Judg 4:14; 2Sam 5:24; Psa 68:8, compare 108:12; 1Chr 14:15; of ׳י‎ going out from Seir Judg 5:14, compare Hab 3:13; of the hand of ׳י‎, in hostility יַדיֿ בִי ׳יָָֽצְאָה‎ Ruth 1:13; absolute of fire breaking out Exod 22:5 (JE).

3 of combinations, note esp.: וָשׁוֺב יָצוֺא‎ (infinitive absolute) Gen 8:7 going out and returning, nearly = to and fro; וּמְקַלֵּל יָצוֺא יֹצֵא ֗֗֗ יוֺצֵא אִישׁ‎ 2Sam 16:5 = coming forth, cursing as he came; ובא יצא‎, literal בָּא וְאֵין יוֺצֵא אֵין‎ Josh 6:1 none went out and none came in, i.e. there was no free egress or ingress (of besieged city), compare 1Kin 15:17 2Chr 16:1; 15:5; to go out and come in before, of leader in war Num 27:17; 1Sam 18:16, compare 29:6; figurative Deut 28:6 blessed shalt thou be ובצאתך בבואך‎, i.e. when thou completest and beginnest any undertaking, so 28:19; 31:2 ולבוא לצאת אוכל לא‎, i.e. I can no more engage in active undertakings; similarly Josh 14:11; 1Kin 3:7; Isa 37:28 ( + שִׁבְתְּךָ‎) = 2Kin 19:27; Psa 121:8.

Hiph`il278 Perfect הוֺצִיא‎ Gen 14:18 +; וְהוֺצִא‎ consecutive Deut 22:14; הוֺצֵאתָ‎ Exod 32:11 7t.; וְהוֺצֵאתָ֫‎ Num 20:8 3t.; 2 feminine singular וְהוֺצֵאת‎ 1Kin 17:13; suffix הוֺצִיאַ֫נִי‎ Ezek 42:15; הוֺצִיאָ֫נוּ‎ Exod 13:14 2t.; הוֺצִיאֲךָ‎ Deut 6:12; 16:1, הוֺצִאֲךָ‎ Exod 13:9; Deut 7:19; הוֺצִיאָם‎ Exod 32:12 2t., etc.; Imperfect יוֺצִיא (יֹצִא)‎ Lev 16:27 9t.; וַיּוֺצֵא (וַיּצֵא)‎ Gen 15:5 23t.; וַיּוֺצִא (וַיֹּצִא)‎ Deut 4:20 4t.; suffix יוֺצִיאֵנִי‎ Micah 7:9; וַיּוֺצִאֲךָ‎ Deut 4:37; 5:15; וַיּוֺצִאָהּ‎ Exod 4:6-7, 3feminine singular תּוֺצִיא‎ Isa 61:11; Hag 1:11; jussive תּוֺצֵא‎ Gen 1:24; וַתּוֺצֵא‎ 1:12; Ruth 2:18; 2masculine singular תּוֺצִיא‎ Exod 12:46 5t.; חֲתֹצִיא‎ Job 38:32; וַתֹּצֵא‎ Jer 32:21; וַיּוֺצִיאוּ (וַיֹּצִאוּ)‎ Lev 24:23 +; suffix וַיּוֺצִיאֻהוּ‎ 2Kin 12:12; וַיֹּצִאֻהוּ‎ Gen 19:16; וַיֹּצִיאֻהוּ‎ 1Kin 21:13; יוֺצִיאוּם‎ 1Chr 9:28, etc.; Imperative הוֺצֵא‎ Gen 19:12 5t. + 8:17 Kt (Qr הַיְצֵא‎); הוֺצִיא‎ Isa 43:8; הוֺצִ֫יאָה‎ Psalm 142:8; suffix הוֺצִיאֵנִי‎ Psa 25:17; 1Kin 22:34, etc.; Infinitive construct הוֺצִיא‎ Exod 6:13 +; suffix הוֺצִיאִי (הוֺצִאִי)‎ 16:32 +; לְהוֺצִאֵהוּ‎ Jer 39:14, anomalous (Köi. 642), etc.; Participle מוֺצִיא‎ Exod 6:7 11t.; מוֺצֵא‎ Psa 135:7; suffix מוֺצִיאִי‎ 2Sam 22:49, מוֺצִיאֲךָ‎ Deut 8:14; 13:11, etc.; —

1 cause to go or come out, bring out, lead out:

a. a person from a place, + מִן‎ local, out of prison, etc. Gen 40:14 (E), Jer 20:3; 52:31 (not || 2Kin 25:27); so with the servant of ׳י‎ subject Isa 42:7; out of house Josh 6:22 (JE), a city Gen 19:12 (J), Ezek 14:22 (so ᵑ9 ᵑ6 ᵐ5‎ Co VB; ᵑ0‎ Hoph`al); of ׳י‎ bringing people of Jerusalem out of city to deliver them to enemy 11:7 (ᵑ0‎ (one) shall bring, but read 1 singular, see VB), 11:9; from a land Jeremiah 26:33; especially of Moses bringing Israelites out of Egypt Exod 3:10-11, 12 (E), 14:11 (J); of Moses and Aaron 6:13, 26, 27 (P); of ׳י‎ bringing Israelites out of (מִן‎) Egypt 18:1; 20:2; Josh 24:6 (all E), Exod 13:3, 9, 14, 16; 32:11; Num 20:16; 23:22; 24:8 (all J E), Deut 1:27; 4:20, 37; 5:6, 15; 6:12, 21, 23; 8:14; 9:12, 26, 28; 13:6; 13:11; 16:1; 26:8 (all D), Lev 19:36; 22:33; 23:43; 25:38, 44, 55; 26:13, 45 (all H), Exod 6:6-7, (מצרים סִבְלֹת מִתַּחַת‎), 7:4-5, 12:17, 42, 51; 16:6, 32; 29:46; Num 15:41 (all P), Judg 2:12; 6:8; 1Sam 12:8; 1Kin 8:16 2Chr 6:5; 1Kin 8:21, 51, 53; 9:9; Jer 7:22; 11:4; 31:32; 32:21; 34:13; Ezek 20:6, 10, compare 20:9 (strike out Co), 2Chr 7:22; Psa 136:11; Dan 9:15; absolute, same sense, Josh 24:5 (E), Deut 7:8, 19; Ezek 20:14, 22; Psa 105:37; 105:43; of ׳י‎ bringing Israelites out of exile (followed by מִן‎) Ezek 20:34, 41; 34:13; object rebels (out of, מִן‎, land) 20:38; of charioteer bringing Ahab out of battle 1Kin 22:34 2Chr 18:33; of Joseph's bringing out his sons from between Jacob's knees Gen 48:12 (E).

b. of bringing from a place for a particular purpose (human subject) Exod 19:17 (מִן‎); also (point of departure not expressed, and purpose sometimes only implied) Gen 38:24 (J), Josh 2:3; 6:23 (twice in verse); Judg 6:30; 2Sam 12:31 = 1Chr 20:3; 2Kin 11:12 2Chr 23:11, 14; Isa 43:8; ׳י‎ subject, of bringing Israelites out of Egypt to slay them Exod 32:16 (JE), Deut 9:28-29, object Gog Ezek 38:4; subject י ׳יַד‎ 37:1.

c. lead out as an army 2Sam 10:16 = 1Chr 19:16, so of ׳י‎ Isa 43:17; hence with הֵבִיא‎, of a ruler's function to lead people out and in 2Sam 5:2 = 1Chr 11:2; Num 27:17 (P).

d. מֵרֶחֶם הוֺצִיא‎ of God's agency in birth Job 10:18.

e. = remove (from a person's presence) מֵעָלָ֑י כָלאִֿישׁ הוֺצִיאוּ‎ Gen 45:1; 2Sam 13:9; without || מעל‎ 13:18.

f. of putting away wives and children Ezra 10:3, 19 (opposed to הוֺשִׁיב‎ 10:2, compare מביתו יצאה‎ Deut 24:2).

g. bring out person unto (אֶל‎) a place (human subject) Josh 10:22-23, (JE), Deut 17:5; 22:21, 24 (all D), Lev 24:14, 23 (H), Num 15:36 (P; all אֶלמִֿחוּץ‎), 1Kin 21:10, 13 (מִחוּץ‎ of motion to), 2Kin 11:15 2Chr 23:14; אֶלהַֿבָּ֑יִת לְהוֺצִאֵהוּ‎ Jer 39:14; subject angels in form of men Gen 19:16-17, (J), Ezek 42:1, 15; 46:21; 47:2; also Gen 15:5 (J E; ׳י‎ subject); for a specific purpose Exod 16:3 (P).

h. unto a person Gen 43:23 (J), with purpose expressed or implied Hosea 9:13; Gen 19:5, 8 (J), Judg 19:22, 24; Josh 10:24 (JE), Jer 38:23; Ezra 8:7 (with על‎) Kt (but read Qr אֲצַוֶּה‎).

i. unto a place and a person Josh 10:22-23, (JE), Deut 21:19; Judg 19:25.

2 figurative, object persons, bring out of (מִן‎) distress, etc. Psa 25:17; 68:7; 107:14; 107:28; Psalm 142:8; 143:11; deliver from enemies 2Sam 22:49 (but || Psa 18:49 מְפַלְּטִי‎); one's feet out of net 25:15; 31:5; bring out into a large place 2Sam 22:20 = Psa 18:20, compare 66:12.

3 bring out animals: horses out of Egypt 1Kin 10:29 2Chr 1:17 (but read

Qal ᵐ5 יֵצְאוּ‎ Klo Kmp in KauAT), 2Chr 1:17; 9:28; animals (from ark, no מן‎) Gen 8:17 (P);for sacrifice, to a place Num 19:3. 4 inanimate object:

a. carry or bring out (with and without מִן‎)Exod 12:39 (E) Amos 6:10; 2Sam 12:30 = 1Chr 20:2; 2Kin 10:26; 23:4, 6; 24:13; 1Chr 9:28; 2Chr 29:5, 16 (twice in verse); 34:14; Jer 8:1; 17:22; 50:25 (subject ׳י‎), Ezek 12:4, 7 (in 12:5; 12:6; 12:7b. 12:12 read

Qal, compare Ezek 12:4b, so Co), also 24:6 (Co 24:10); object הָראֹשָׁה הָאֶבֶן‎ Zech 4:7; Lev 26:10 (H), Ezra 1:7 (twice in verse); 1:8.

b. take or draw out (from one's person or luggage) Gen 24:53 (J); draw out hand from one's bosom Exod 4:6-7, (J), compare Ruth 2:18 (food from one's cupboard).

c. = draw מִתַּעְרָ֑הּ חַרְבִּי‎ Ezek 21:8; 21:10 (subject ׳י‎).

d. bring outto a place Deut 28:38; Lev 4:12, 21; 6:4; 14:45; 16:27 Ezek 46:20, compare Deut 14:28.

e. bring out to (or for) a person Gen 14:18; Judg 6:19 compare 6:18, 1Kin 17:13; 2Kin 10:22 (twice in verse).

f. bring out from (מִן‎) a place to people Numbers 17:24 (P).

g. bring out in payment, pay (money, tribute, etc.) 2Kin 12:12; 15:20 (עַל‎ = in behalf of: or put it forth, imposed it, on Israel).

h. bring forth (= cause to rise or appear) the heavenly bodies Isa 40:26; Job 38:32; see also אוֺר יֹצִא וְתַעֲלֻמָה‎ 28:11 and hidden things he (the miner) bringeth forth tolight.

i. bring forth by miracle: Moses. water out of rock Num 20:8, 10 (JE); ׳י‎ id. Deut 8:15; Neh 9:15; Psa 78:16.

j. = produce, Generate, bring into being: of magicians trying to produce lice Exod 8:14 (P); a smith producing weapon Isa 54:16; see the threefold הוציא‎ Prov 30:33 (3 t. in verse); of ׳י‎ causing לֶחֶם‎ to proceed out of (מִן‎) earth Psa 104:14; elsewhere of earth as producing Gen 1:12, 24 (both P), Isa 61:11; Hag 1:11; of Aaron's rod bringing forth blossoms Numbers 17:28 (P).

k. bring forth words (out of mouth, etc.), i.e. speak Job 8:10; 15:3; Prov 10:18; 29:11; Neh 6:19; Isa 48:20 (|| השׁמיע הגיד,‎); absolute Eccl 5:1; of publishing a report ׳הו רָ֑ע שֵׁם עָלֶיהָ‎ Deut 22:14 (|| דְּבָרִים עֲלִילֹת לָהּ שָׂם‎) compare 22:19; ׳הו רָעָהׅ ( הָאָרֶץ דִּבַּת‎ Num 13:32; 14:37; so 14:36 (עַלהָֿאָרֶץ דִּבָּה‎).

5 figurative, subject ׳י‎, bring forth from (מִן‎) Bel's mouth what he has swallowed Jeremiah 5:44; wind, out of treasuries Jer 10:13; 51:16; Psa 135:7; fire, out of Tyre Ezek 28:18; curse, over the land Zech 5:4; of Jeremiah, יָקָר תּוֺצִיא אִם מִזּוֺלֵל‎ Jer 15:19 if thou bring forth the precious from (Gie without) the base, i.e. if thou free that which is pure in thee from base admixture (Gf; Gie if thou produce the noble without the base); bring forth, i.e. exhibit, righteousness (nnocence Che) Psa 37:6; Jer 51:10 (compare Qal 1 f end); צַלְמָוֶת לָאוֺר וַיֹּצֵא‎ Job 12:22, compare Micah 7:9; subject servant of ׳י‎ of publishing מִשְׁמָּט‎ (i.e. religion) to the world Isa 42:1, 3.

Hoph`al Perfect3feminine singular הוּצָ֑אָה‎ Ezek 38:8 (strike out Co); Participle feminine singular מוּצֵאת‎ Gen 38:25; masculine plural מוּצָאִים‎ 14:22; 47:8 (but see below); feminine plural מוּצָאוֺת‎ Jer 38:22; — be brought forth Gen 38:25 (J; of Tamar); of women as captives Jer 38:22; remnant out of Jerusalem Ezek 14:22 ᵑ0‎ (but read Hiph`il, see above); exiles, from among the peoples 38:8 (omitted by ᵑ6‎ Co); of waters, הַמּוּצָאִים אֶלהַֿיָּ֫מָּה‎ 47:8 which are caused to flow into the sea (but ᵑ6‎ Co הַחֲמוּאִים אֶלהַֿמַּיִם‎ into the sour (bitter, salt) waters, see Field VB).

צאה.def:
ו‎

ו‎, Waw, sixth letter; in modern Hebrew = numeral 6; no evidence of this usage in OT times.

וָ וּ, וְ,‎

demonstrative adverb and

conjunction so, then, and (Phoenician, Moabite, Aramaic ו‎; Arabic ; Ethiopic Assyrian u DlW (but between verbs the usually connective is the enclitic ma KAT2. 508, Dl§§ 82, 150). The use in Hebrew shews that original וְ‎ was not a merely copulative conjunction, but that it possessed a demonstrative force (compare Dr§ 122), which is often perceptible as such, though in other cases, from its being applied to denote mere juxtaposition or connection [compare Greek τε, and Latin tum .... tum = 'both .... and,' both properly demonstratives: Assyrian ma has also a demonstrative force, Dl§ 79], it is less palpable) — וְ‎ before shwa' mobile or a labial is vocalized וּ‎; often before a tone-syll., when the word itself has a disj. accent, וָ‎ (as וַָמתִּי׃‎ Gen 19:19; וָמֵ֖תוּ‎ 33:13; וָמֵ֑ת‎ 44:9; וָחָֽיָה׃‎ Exod 1:16; וָיָ֑מָּה‎ Josh 15:46; וָ֔לֹ֕א‎ 2Sam 13:26; וָאָ֖רֶץ‎ Isa 26:19; וָקָ֔מוּ‎ 49:7; וָחָֽתָּה׃‎ Jer 48:1; וָרָֹע‎ Psa 10:15); especially when it forms with the preceding word a pair, whether of parallel or opposed ideas (as וָכֹה כֹּה‎ Exod 2:12, וָמִ֖י מִי‎ 10:8, וָאָ֑בֶן אֶבֶן‎ Deut 25:13; וָדֹ֑ר דֹּר‎ 32:7 +; וָבֹ֔הוּ תֹּהוּ‎ Gen 1:2, וָרֶמֶ֛שׂ בְּהֵמָה‎ 1:24, וָרָֽע׃ טוֺב‎ 2:19, וָנָ֖ד נָע‎ 4:12, וָלָ֖יְלָה וְיוֺם וָחֹ֛רֶף וְקַיִץ‎ 8:22, וֵָלךְ׃ קַח‎ 12:19, וָאָֽרֶץ׃ שָׁמַיִם‎ 14:19, וָאָ֑תָּה אֲנִי‎ 31:44, וָה֑וּא אֲנִי‎ 41:11, וָשׁוּבוּ עִבְרוּ‎ Exod 32:27, וָהֵ֛ם אַתָּה‎ Num 16:16, וָמֶ֑לָךְ אֱלֹהִים‎ 1Kin 21:13, וָנֶ֖כֶד נִין‎ Isa 14:22, וָשֶׁ֖בֶר שֹׁד‎ 59:7; and often: see more fully Bö§ 600); occasionally also with a conjunctive accent (as לְעֹלָֽם׃ וָשַחי‎ Gen 3:22 compare Lev 18:5, שָׁם וָמַ֣תְנוּ‎ 2Kin 7:4, חֲדָשָׁ֑ה וָאָ֣רֶץ‎ Isa 65:17; Prov 25:3, גָּדוֺל׃ וָשֶשׁבֶר שֹׁ֖ד‎ Jer 48:3, compare 32:29). — וְ‎ is used very freely and widely in Hebrew, but also with much delicacy, to express relations and shades of meaning which Western languages would usually indicate by distinct particles. But in Hebrew particles such as לָכֵן לְמַעַן, בַּעֲבוּר, אוּלָם, אָכֵן, אַךְ, אָז, אוֺ,‎, etc., were reserved for cases in which special emphasis or distinctness was desired: their frequent use was felt instinctively to be inconsistent with the lightness and grace of movement which the Hebrew ear loved; and thus in AV, RV, words like or, then, but, notwithstanding, howbeit, so, thus, therefore, that, constantly appear, where the Hebrew has simply וְ‎.

1 And, connecting both words (see above), and sentences (Gen 1:5 וג קָרָא ׳וְלַחשֶׁךְ‎). When three, four, or more words follow, the conjunction may connect them all, as 7:21; 10:2 (6 t.) 24:35 (7 t.) Josh 7:24 (10 t.) 2Sam 17:28f.: often however it is prefixed only to the last, as Gen 5:32; 10:1; Deut 18:10 etc.; occas. even it connects only the first two, 1Kin 8:47; Isa 1:13; Psa 45:9; Job 42:9. Remarkably, however, וְ‎ as a mere conjunction is, as a rule, not in classical Hebrew attached directly to verbs (especially in the perfect), the construction with וְ‎ consecutive (see

2) being (as in Moabite) preferred: thus וַיִּבֶן יָצָא‎ is said, not וּבָנָה יָצָא‎. Exceptions in classical Hebrew are (a) sometimes where synonyms are coupled, as Num 23:19 וְדִבֶּר ֗֗֗ אָמַר‎, Deut 2:30; Judg 5:26; 1Sam 12:2; Isa 1:2 ורוממתי גדּלתי‎ 2:11; 5:14; 8:8; 19:6; 29:20; (b) isolated cases, difficult to reduce to rule (perhaps sometimes due to textual error), as Gen 28:6; 38:5; Judg 3:23; 7:13; 16:18; 1Sam 1:12; 3:13; 4:19; 5:7; 10:9; 17:38, 48; 25:20 and elsewhere (in other passages, apparently similar, the perfect and וְ‎ has a frequent. force (see 2), as Gen 37:3; Exod 36:29f.; Num 10:17f. 21:15, 20; 1Sam 2:22; 16:14; 17:34f. (see Dr) 27:9; 2Sam 16:13; 17:17, perhaps also Gen 15:6; 21:25; 34:5). In later parts of OT, probably through Aramaic influence, the perfect with simple וְ‎ occurs more frequently: so especially in Ecclesiastes, where it is all but universal (e.g. 2:11-12, 13, 15 etc.). With the imperfect, the simple וְ‎ is not so unidiomatic, even in classical Hebrew (compare 3); see 1:9, 26; 9:27; 17:2; 22:17; 27:29; Exod 23:8 (frequently) 24:7; Num 14:12; Deut 17:13; 30:12-13, Josh 3:13; 7:3; Judg 7:3; 13:8; Isa 5:29; 14:10; often also in Jeremiah, Isa2, Job, Psalms, e.g. 40:30; 41:20 (Dr§ 116: contrast 28:13). See more fully Dr§ 130-4 Ges§ 112. 6. Special senses: —

a. it sometimes = and specially, Gen 3:16; 1Kin 11:1 many strange women, and specially the daughter of Pharaoh, Isa 1:1 Judah and (= and particularly) Jerusalem, 2:1; 9:7; Psa 18:1.

b. and in particular ('und zwar'), and that (explicative), Gen 4:4; Judg 7:22; 1Sam 17:40 וּבַיַּלְקוּט‎, 28:3 in Ramah, and that in his city (unusual: text suspicious), 2Sam 13:20 וְשֹׁמֵמָה‎ and that desolate, Isa 57:11 I have been silent וּמֵעוֺלָם‎ and that from of old, 32:7; Jer 15:13; Amos 3:11 (si vera lectio), 4:10; Zech 9:9b Mal 1:11; Psa 68:10; Prov 3:12; Lam 3:26; Eccl 8:2; Dan 1:3; 8:10; 9:25, 27; Neh 8:13; 1Chr 9:27; 2Chr 8:13; 29:27 (but' even' for ו‎, before ל‎ and infinitive, e.g. in Isa 44:28; Jer 17:10; 19:12, is wrong; see Ew§ 351 c, Dr§ 206).

c. sometimes it introduces an idea which so exceeds or adds to what has preceded, that it is nearly equivalent to also, 1Sam 25:43; 1Kin 2:22 ask also the kingdom for him; unusually Hosea 8:6 והוא מישׂראל כי‎ for of Israel is it also, Eccl 5:6 והבלים‎ (see De) 2Chr 27:5 (but see ᵐ5‎). Or it may be rendered yea: so especially in the ascending numerations 3-4 Amos 1:3, 6, 9, 11, 13; 2:1, 4, 6; Prov 30:18, 21, 29, 6-7 6:16; Job 5:19, 7-8 Micah 5:4 — the first number being aggravated, or augmented, by a higher. In one idiom וּגְבוּל‎, occurring in geographic descriptions, it is used peculiarly, seemingly = at the same time: Num 34:6 and as for the western border, וּגְבוּל הַגָּדוֺל הַיָּם לָכֶם וְהָיָה‎ the great sea shall be to you also (German 'zugleich') a border, Deut 3:16 וּגְבוּל הַנַּחַל תּוֺךְ‎ the middle of the stream being at the same time the border, 3:17; Josh 13:23, 27; 15:12, 47 (but these, except Num 34:6, might be cases of 5c γ).

d. it connects alternative cases, so that it = or: Exod 20:10, 17; 21:16 he that stealeth a man בְיָדוֺ וְנִמְצָא וּמְכָרוֺ‎ and selleth him, and (= or if) he be found in his hand, 21:17; Lev 21:14; 22:23-24, Prov 29:9 (Fl Ew RV: whether . . . or) Job 31:13, 16, 26, etc.

e. it connects contrasted ideas, where in our idiom the contrast would be expressed explicitly by but; in such cases prominence is usually given to the contrasted idea by its being placed immediately after the conjunction: Gen 2:17 but of the tree of the knowledge . . . thou shalt not eat, 4:2, 5; 6:8; 17:21; 31:10 etc., 1Kin 2:26; 10:7; 11:32, 34; 15:14; Prov 10:1-2, 3, 4 + often; even after לֹא‎ (where כִּי‎ or אִם כִּי‎ might be expected), as Gen 42:10; Exod 21:18; Lev 26:45; Deut 11:11; Judg 19:12; 1Kin 3:11.

f. it introduces a contrasted idea in such a way as to suggest a question, especially before a pronoun, Judg 14:16 I told it not to my father or my mother, אַגִּיד וְלָךְ‎ and shall I told it unto thee? 2Sam 11:11; Jer 25:29 תִנָּקוּ הִנָּקֵה וְאַתֶּם‎ and shall ye be guiltless? 45:5; Ezek 20:31; 33:25b Jonah 4:11. So the וְ‎ consecutive and perfect (see 2a), Exod 5:5 וְהִשְׁבַּתֶּם‎ and will ye make them rest from their burdens? Num 16:10 וּבִקַּשְׁתֶּם‎ and seek ye the priesthood also? 1Sam 25:11; Isa 66:9; Psa 50:21 and shall I keep silence? Job 32:16 (compare Dr§ 119 γ).

g. attaching a fresh subj. (or object) to a clause already grammatically complete, it = and also, Gen 2:9b Num 16:2, 18 and they stood at the entrance of the tent of meeting, ואהרן ומשׁה‎ and Moses and Aaron (stood also), 16:27; Exod 35:22; Judg 6:5; Gen 1:16; b 12:17; 44:2; 46:15; Exod 29:3; Jer 32:29 (compare DrSm. i. 6, 11, & p. 293): when the idea thus attached is subordinate, or not logically embraced in the principal predicate, it approximates to the Arabic or 'waw of association' (followed by an accusative: WAG ii. § 37), Est 4:16 אָצוּם וְנַעֲרֹתַי אֲנִי‎ I will fast (singular) and (= with) my maidens, Exod 21:4; 1Sam 25:42; 29:10b (but insert here אַתָּה‎ with ᵐ5‎) 2Sam 12:30 (but read וּבָהּ‎, as 1Chr 20:2) 1Sam 20:10; Neh 6:12; Gen 4:20; Isa 42:5; Jer 19:1 (but read מזקני וְלָקַחְתָּ֫‎ with ᵐ5‎) 2Chr 2:3; 13:11; compare Jer 22:7 (וְכֵלָיו אִישׁ‎), Job 41:12. Whether Isa 48:16 וְרוּחוֺ‎ belongs here, is dubious

h. וְ‎ repeated = both . . . and (but גַּם ֗֗֗ גַּם‎) is more usual in this sense); Gen 34:28; Num 9:14; Josh 9:23; 2Sam 5:8 (text dubious), Isa 16:5; 38:15; Jer 13:14; 21:6; 32:14 (text dubious) 32:20; 40:8; Psa 76:7; Job 34:29; Dan 8:13; Neh 12:28.

i. a repetition of the same word with וְ‎ interposed expresses (a) diversity (rare), Deut 25:13 וָאֶבֶן אֶבֶן‎ a weight and a weight, i.e. different weights (explained by וּקְטַנָּה גְּדֹלָה‎), 25:14; Prov 20:23; Psa 12:3 וָלֵב בְּלֵב‎ with a heart and a heart = with a double heart, 1Chr 12:33 וָלֵב לֵב בְּלֹא‎; (b) distribution (except in וָדֹר דֹּר‎ Deut 32:7; Isa 13:20 +?Intr. 505) Psa 87:5; 1Chr 26:13 וָשָֽׁעַר׃ לְשַׁעַר‎ = for every gate, 28:14 (twice in verse); 2Chr 8:14; 34:13; 35:15; Ezra 10:14 וָעִיר עִיר זִקְנֵי‎ elders of every city, Neh 13:24; Est 1:8, 22 (twice in verse); 2:12; 3:4, 12 (4 t. in verse); 8:9 (twice in verse); strengthened by כָּלֿ‎2Chr 11:12 ועיר עיר בכל‎ in every several city, 19:5; 28:25; 31:19; 32:28; Est 2:11 ויום בכליֿום‎, 3:14; 4:3; 8:11, 13, 17 (twice in verse); 9:21, 27, 28; Psalm 45:18; Psa 145:13 (common in post-Biblical Hebrew, especially with כל‎).

j. it is used in the formulation of proverbs (the Vav adaequationis, הִשְׁתַּוָּאָה וָו‎) as Prov 17:3; 25:3, 20, 25 cold waters to a thirsty soul and good news from a far country (i.e. they are like each other), 26:3, 9, 14, 20; 27:21; Eccl 5:2; 7:1; 8:8; compare 9:11; Psa 19:5; 125:2; Job 14:11f.; 14:19 (compare in Arabic 'every man and his cares [accusative],' 'every thing and its price,' i.e. they go together: 'merchants and dogs [accusative] of Seleucia,' i.e. they are like one another: see FlKl. Schr. iii. 535 f.). More rarely in the opposite order, 5:7; 12:11. But 1Sam 12:15b cannot be thus explained: read with וּבְמַלְכְּכֶם ᵐ5‎, and see Dr.

k. in circumstantial clauses וְ‎ introduces a statement of the concomitant conditions under which the action denoted by the principal verb takes place: in such cases, the relation expressed by וְ‎ must often in English be stated explicitly by a conjunction, as when, since, seeing, though, etc., as occasion may require. So very often, as Gen 11:4 let us build a tower בַשָּׁמַיִם וְראֹשׁוֺ‎ and its top in the heavens (= with its top in etc.), 18:12 shall I have pleasure, זָקֵן וַאדֹנִי‎ and my lord is old (= my lord being old)? Judg 16:15 How sayest thou, I love thee, אִתִּי אֵין וְלִבְּךָ‎ and (= when) thy heart is not with me? and especially with a person pronoun, Gen 15:2 what wilt thou give me עֲרִירִי הֹלֵךְ וְאָנֹכִי‎ and I (= the case being that I) am going hence childless? 18:13; 20:3 lo, thou wilt die because of the woman thou hast taken בָּֽעַל׃ בְּעֻלַת וְהִוא‎ = seeing she is married, 24:62 ישֵׁב וְהוּא‎ = since or for he was dwelling (different from וַיֵּשֶׁב‎ = and he proceeded to dwell), 26:27 וְאַתֶּם‎ seeing ye hate me, Judg 13:9 and came to her ישֶׁבֶת וְהִיא‎ = as she was sitting, 1Sam 18:23; 1Kin 19:19 +? Psa 72:12 the afflicted לוֺ וְאֵיןעֹֿזֵר‎ and (= when) he has no helper (compare Job 29:12), Job 104:25 מִסְמָּר וְאֵין‎, Job 105:34; 5:9. See more fully Dr§ 156-60 Ges§ 141, R 2. (The analogous use of the is very common in Arabic: Wii. § 183.) Introducing an appeal to a fact confirmatory of some statement or promise, it almost = as truly as (compare Ew§ 340 c) Hosea 12:6 and J. is God of hosts, J. is his name! Joel 4:20; Amos 9:5-6 Isa 51:15 and I [who promise this] am J. thy God, who . . . . ! Jer 29:23; Psa 89:38b (compare in Qoran the frequently 'And God is .. . . . [the mighty, the merciful, etc.]').

2 The ו‎ consecutive (formerly called the Waw 'conversive'); —

a. with the

imperfect (וַּ‎ with following daghesh; before וָ א,‎), as וַיּאֹמֶר‎ properly = and he proceeded to say, chiefly in contin. of a preceding perfect tense (so Moabite);

b. with the

perfect (וְ‎, — in 1 & 2 singular, the tone, with certain exceptions [see Dr§ 110], being thrown forward to the ultima), as וְיָָֽשַׁבְתָּ֫‎ properly so [namely, as limited by a verb, or other term, preceding] hadst thou sat, chiefly in continuation of a preceding imperfect tense, in its various senses of future, jussive, or frequentative. Thefurther analysis of these idioms belongs to the grammar; see on a DrCh. vi., Ges§ 111, and on

b DrCh. viii. Ges§ 112. Here it must suffice to note — (a) ו‎ consecutive (especially with the imperfect) frequently couples two verbs in such a manner that the first, indicating the general character of the action, receives its closer definition in the second: in such cases, the first may often be represented in English by an adverb, as Gen 26:18 וַיַּחְמֹּר וַיָּשָׁב‎ and he turned and dug = and he dug again; so often; and similarly with הוֺסִיף‎ 25:1, מִהַר‎ 24:18, הוֺאִיל‎ Josh 7:7, etc.; more exceptionally, Gen 30:27; Est 8:6, and (not consecutive) Gen 47:6; Job 23:3; Song 2:3; Lam 3:26 (see Ges§ 120, 2 a; compare in Syriac Nö§ 335-6. In Arabic the stronger form of the conjugation here corresponds: Wii. § 140). (b) וַּ ‎ with the imperfect sometimes expresses a contrast = and yet, Gen 32:31 I have seen God face to face וַתִּנָּצֵל‎ and yet my soul is delivered, Deut 4:33; 2Sam 3:8; 19:29; Isa 51:12; Psa 73:14; 144:3; Job 10:8 + (compare Dr§ 74 β). (c) there is a tendency in the later books of the OT to use the perfect with simple וְ‎, where the classical language would employ the imperfect with וַּ ‎ (compare above

1); so especially in Ecclesiastes, where וַּ ‎ occurs thrice only, Job 1:17; 4:1, 7. (d) a double perfect with ו‎ consecutive is sometimes used, informally but neatly, with a hypothetical force; thus (a) in past or present time Exod 16:21 וְנָמָֽס׃ הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ וְחַם‎ and the sun used to be warm, and it used to melt = and if (or when) the sun was warm, it melted, 33:10; 1Kin 18:10; Jer 18:4, 8 וְנִחַמְתִּ֫י וְֹשָׁב‎ = and if it turns, I repent, 20:9 (see RV); (β) in future time, Gen 44:22 ומת אביו ועזב‎ and he will leave his father, and he will die = and if he leaves his father, he will die, 33:13; 42:38; Exod 4:14; 12:13; 1Sam 16:2; 19:3; Ezek 33:3; 39:15 etc. (Dr§ 147-9, Ges§ 159. 2 e).

3 With a

voluntative (cohortative or jussive) וְ‎ expresses an intention, that or so that (an elegancy by which the too frequent use of לְמַעַן‎ or בַּעֲבוּר‎ is avoided): Exod 10:17 entreat God, וְיָסֵר‎ so may he remove (= that he may remove) this death, Gen 27:4 and bring it me וְאֹכֵ֑לָה‎ so let me eat (= that I may eat); and without the modal form being externally indicated, Exod 14:1 speak . . . וְיָשֻׁבוּ‎ that they return, 14:15; and often Sts. even of past time, as 1Kin 13:33 whom he would, he consecrated וִיהִי‎ that there might be priests of the high places, 2Kin 19:25; Isa 25:9 a Lam 1:19. After a negative, Psa 51:18 thou desirest not sacrifice, וְאֶתֵּ֑נָה‎ so [= in that case] would I give it (or, that I might give it), 55:13 וְאֶשָּׂא‎ so could I bear it (or, that I might bear it), Isa 53:2 RVm Num 23:19; Jer 5:28 RV. Sts. also before an imperative, Gen 12:2 and be (= that thou mayest be) a blessing, 2Sam 21:3 +. See more fully Dr§ 59-65, Ges§ 108. 2; 109. 2; 110. 2. (In Arabic with the subjunctive is used similarly: Wii. § 15 d.) A volunt. is also sometimes attached by וְ‎ to a preceding volunt. or imperative, so as to form a virtually hypothetical sentence, as Gen 42:18 וִחְיוּ עֲשׂוּ זֹאת‎ = if you do this, you shall live, 30:28; 34:12; Prov 3:9f. 4:4, 8; Isa 55:2: see Dr§ 152.

4 It expresses often an informal inference, or consequence, so, then, especially at the beginning of a speech: Gen 27:8; Psa 2:10 and often וְעַתָּה‎ now, therefore; וְלָמָּה‎ and וּמַדּוּעַ‎ why, then? Gen 29:25; Num 12:8; 16:3 +; Exod 2:20 וְאַיּוֺ‎ where, then, is he? Gen 34:21; 1Sam 15:14; 26:22 וְיַעֲבֹר‎ let, then, . . . come over, 2Sam 24:3; 2Kin 4:41 קֶמַח וּקְחוּ‎ then bring meal, Ezek 18:32. So the וְ‎ consecutive and the perfect, as Deut 2:4 וְנִשְׁמַרְתֶּם‎ take heed, therefore, 4:15; 7:9 וְיָָֽדַעְתָּ֫‎ know, therefore, 30:19; 1Sam 6:5; 1Kin 2:6; Ruth 3:9; Josh 15:19; Isa 40:6b (Dr§ 119 δ).

5 ו‎ introduces the predicate or apodosis: namely

a. וְ‎ consecutive and the Perfect — in answer to אִם‎ or כִּי‎ constantly, as Exod 19:5; 23:22 if thou hearkenest to my voice, וְאָֽיַבְתִּ֫י‎ then am I (= I will be) enemy to thy enemies (see Dr§ 136-8); after the casus pendens, 12:44 every servant that is bought for money, וּמַלְתָּ֫ה‎ thou shalt circumcise him, etc. Num 14:31; 24:24; 1Sam 25:27; 2Sam 14:10 he that spake unto thee, אֵלַי וַהֲבֵאתוֺ‎ so hast thou brought him (= thou shalt bring him) unto me, Isa 9:4; 56:6f. +; Exod 12:15; 31:14; Deut 17:12 +; after various time-determinations, as Gen 3:5 in the day of your eating from it וְנִפְקְחוּ‎ then shall your eyes be opened, Exod 16:6 וִידַעְתֶּם עֶרֶב‎ at even, then shall ye know, 16:7; 32:34; 2Sam 15:10; 1Kin 13:31 אֹתִי וּקְבַרְתֶּם בְּמוֺתִי‎ when I die, so ye shall bury me, etc., + often; after conjs., as כִּי‎ Gen 29:15, יַעַן‎ 1Kin 20:28; Isa 3:16f., תַּחַת‎ 60:15, etc., (see Dr§ 123).

b. וַּ ‎ consecutive and the imperfect (but much less frequently than the perfect), as Gen 30:30 the little that thou hadst, וַיִּפְרֹץ‎ it hath increased, Exod 9:21; 2Sam 4:10; 1Kin 9:20f. 15:13 +; after time-determinations, Gen 22:4 on the third day וַיִּשָּׂא‎ then Abraham lifted up his eyes, 19:15; 27:34; 37:18; 1Sam 6:6; 12:8; Isa 6:1; Hosea 11:1 when Israel was a child, וָאֹהֲבֵהוּ‎ then I loved him, +; occasionally after conjunctions, as כַּאֲשֶׁר‎ Exod 16:34, יַעַן‎ 1Sam 15:23, לְמַעַן‎ Isa 45:4, אִם‎ Psa 59:16 (Dr§ 127).

c. in other cases (not 'consecutive') — all more or less uncommon: namely a. וְ‎ closely joined to the imperfect Gen 13:9 if to the left, וְאֵימִינָה‎ then I will take the right (compare 2Sam 12:8) Exod 12:3 on the 10th of the month וְיִקְחוּ‎ then let them take, Num 16:5; Isa 43:4; Hosea 4:6; 10:10; Psa 69:33; Job 15:17; 2Sam 22:41; Prov 23:24 Kt (Dr§ 125); β. separated from the verb, Exod 8:22; Lev 7:16 יֵאָכֵל וְהַנּוֺתָר וּמִמָּחֳרָת‎ and on the morrow, then the remainder shall be eaten, Josh 3:3; 1Kin 8:32; Isa 8:7; 48:7; Job 14:7; 20:18; b 23:12; 25:5; 32:14 +; γ. without a verb, Gen 40:9 וְהִנֵּה בַּחֲלֹמִי‎ in my dream, behold, a vine was before me, 40:16; 2Sam 23:3f.; Prov 10:25, and the extreme cases 2Sam 15:34 thy father's slave, מֵאָז וַאֲנִי‎ I was that of old, — but now עַבְדְּךָ וַאֲנִי‎ well, I will be thine, Isa 34:12 (si vera lectio), Job 4:6b דְּרָכֶיךָ וְתֹם תִּקְוָָֽתְךָ‎ thy confidence — it is the uprightness of thy ways, 36:26 חֵקֶר וְלֹא שָׁנָיו מִסְמַּר‎ Ges. seine Jahre, da ist kein Zählen (compare Dr§ 124-5, 128-9). — With 4, 5 compare the Arabic , Wi. § 366 b, 367 c; ii. § 187; Dr§ 185 end.

H6629. tson

צאֹן‎273 collective noun feminineGen 30:36 (possibly masculine 30:39 a +, KöSynt. § 247 g, but dubious, 30:39b with verb feminine plural, as usually; in 1Sam 15:14 join הַוֶּה‎ with קוֺל‎; see further AlbrZAW xv (1895), 316 ff.) small cattle, sheep and goats, flock, flocks; — ׳צ‎ absolute Gen 4:2 +; construct 29:9 +; suffix צאֹנוֺ‎ 4:4 +; צאֹנֵנוּ‎ Exod 10:9, צאֹונֵוּ‎ Psa 144:13; as plural צאֹנֵינוֺ‎ Neh 10:37 van d. H. Gi (not Baer; very late, si vera lectio), etc.; —

a. small cattle, usually of sheep and goats in one flock (RobBR i. 477) Gen 30:31-32, +; sheep specified also 21:28 (הַצּ ׳כִּבְשׂת‎), 31:28 (צ ׳אֵילֵי‎) +; sheep only 1Sam 25:2 (+עִוִּים‎); goats specified Gen 27:9; Jer 50:8; ׳צ‎ as yielding (1) animals for food Amos 6:4 (בָּרִים‎), 1Sam 14:32; 2Sam 12:4; Neh 5:18 +; ׳צ מַאְַבָל‎ Psa 44:12 (in simile); (2) wool Gen 31:19 + (see [ גָּזַז‎], גֵּז‎); (3) milk, צ ׳חֲלֵב‎ Deut 32:14 (? goats' milk, compare Prov 27:27); (4) sacrificial victims Gen 4:4 (J), Lev 1:2, 10; 3:6; Num 15:3 (all P), 22:40 (E), Deut 12:6, 17, 21 + often; so קָדָשִׁים צאֹן‎ Ezek 36:38 a, compare בְּכוֺרֵי וְצאֹנֵינוּ בְקָרֵינוּ‎ Neh 10:37; in General as property (often + בָּקָר‎, etc.) Gen 12:16; 13:5; 24:35; Job 1:3; 42:12 + often (see also II. H6643. tsbiy

I. צְבִי‎ noun masculine2Sam 1:19 beauty, honour; — absolute ׳צ‎ 1:19 +, צֶבִ֑י‎ Dan 8:9; construct צְבִי‎ Isa 13:19 +; plural construct צִבְאוֺת‎ Jer 3:19 (so ᵑ7‎ Ki Thes Hi Gf Ol § 145 b Köii.l, 584 and others; > from ᵑ6 צבא‎ Gie and others); —

b. elsewhere in figure: of drunkard's chaplet, ׳צ תִפְאַרְתּוֺ‎ Isa 28:1, 4 (figurative of Samaria); צ ׳עֲטֶרֶת‎ 28:5 (of ׳י‎); ׳הַצּ‎ 2Sam 1:19 (Saul and Jonathan); כָּלצֿ ׳גְּאוֺן‎, of Tyre Isa 23:9; ׳צ מַמְלָכוֺת‎ 13:19 (of Babylonian ); of land of Israel (Judah), לְכָלהָֿאֲרָצוֺת הִיא צְבִי‎ Ezek 20:6, 15, צִבְאוֺת צְבִי נַחֲלַת גּוֺיִם‎ Jer 3:19 (see above) heritage of the beauty of beauties of the nations, i.e. most beauteous heritage; ׳הַצּ‎ especially of Jerusalem and temple Dan 8:9 (Bev), compare הַצּ ׳אֶרֶץ‎ 11:16, 41 (see Dr), צ קֹֿרֶשׁ׳הַר‎ 11:45(i.e. temple-hill); of cities of Moab, ׳צ אֶרֶץ‎ Ezek 25:9.

1 what is right, just, normal; rightness, justness, of weights and measures, וָצֶדֶק שְׁלֵמָה אֶבֶן אֵיפָה,‎ Deut 25:15 a perfect and a just weight, ephah; צ ׳מאֹזְנֵי‎; צ ׳בַּת צ, ׳הִין צ, ׳אֵיפַת צ, ׳אַבְנֵי‎ Lev 19:36 (H) Job 31:6; Ezek 45:10; צ ׳מַעְגְּלֵי‎ right paths Psa 23:3; צ ׳זִבְחֵי‎ right peace-offerings Deut 33:19; Psa 4:6; Psalm 51:21.

2 righteousness, in government:

a. of judges, rulers, kings, בצ ׳שׁפט‎ Lev 19:15(H); צ ׳שׁפט‎ Deut 1:16; Prov 31:9; צ ׳משׁפט‎ Deut 16:18; צ ׳רדף‎ 16:20; צ ׳חוֺקֵק‎ Prov 8:15; לצ ׳מלך‎ Isa 32:1; צ ׳דבּר‎ Psa 58:2; also Prov 25:5; Psa 94:15; Eccl 5:7.

b. of law, as מִשְׁמָּטִים‎ Isa 58:2; Psa 119:7; 119:62; 119:75; 119:106; 119:160 (ᵐ5‎, but מִשְׁמַּט ᵑ0‎), 119:164; as עֵדוֺת‎ 119:138; 119:144; as מִצְוֺר‎ 119:172.

c. of Davidic king, Messiah Isa 11:4-5, 16:5; Psa 45:5, דצ ׳דין‎ 72:2.

d. of Jerusalem, as seat of just government, הַצֶּדֶק עִיר‎ Isa 1:26 city of righteousness; צ ׳נְוֵה‎ Jer 31:23; 50:7 (possibly these reflect an original god צֶדֶק‎, see צֶדֶק מַלְכִּי‎); ׳צ בָּהּ יָלִין‎ Isa 1:21 righteousness used to lodge in her; compare הצ ׳מְקוֺם‎ Eccl 3:16 the place of righteousness.

e. of God's attribute as sovereign Job 36:3, husband of Israel Hosea 2:21; ׳צ‎ his personified agent Psa 85:11; 85:12; Psalm 85:14, foundation of his throne 89:15 = 97:2; in his government 9:9; 65:6; 96:13 = 98:9, promise Isa 45:19, administration of justice Job 8:3; Jer 11:20; Psalm 7:18; Psa 48:11; 50:6 = 97:6, vindication of his people 9:5; 35:24; 35:28; raising up Cyrus Isa 45:13, calling his servant 42:6; צִדְקִי אֱלֹהֵי‎ Psa 4:2 God of my righteousness (who vindicates me); his ׳צ‎ is everlasting 119:142.

3 righteousness, justice, in a case or cause Job 6:29; 8:6; 29:14; Psa 35:27; Isa 59:4; God כצ ׳שׁפט‎ Psa 7:9 judges according to righteousness; כצ ׳גמל‎ 18:21; כצ ׳השׁיב‎ 18:25; צ ׳שׁמע‎ 17:1 צ ׳הוציא‎ 37:6.

4 rightness, in speech, צ ׳דבּר‎ Psa 52:5 (opposed to שֶׁקֶר‎); צ ׳יַגִּיד‎ Prov 12:17; ׳בצ פי אמרי כל‎ 8:8; צ ׳שִׂפְתֵי‎ 16:13.

5 righteousness, as ethically right Job 35:2; Psa 17:15; 45:8; Prov 1:3; 2:9; Eccl 7:15; Jer 22:13; Ezek 3:20; Hosea 10:12 (read צ ׳מְּרִי‎, so ᵐ5‎ We Now); עלמים׳צ‎ Dan 9:24; צ ׳עשׂה‎ Isa 64:4; Psa 119:121; צ ׳פעל‎ 15:2; צ ׳למד‎ Isa 26:6, 10; צ ׳בקּשׁ‎ Zeph 2:3; צ ׳רדף‎ Isa 51:1; צ ׳ידע‎ 51:7.

6 righteousness as vindicated, justification in controversy with enemies and troubles, deliverance, victory, prosperity:

a. of God as covenant-keeping, in redemption, צִדְקִי בִּימִין‎ Isa 41:10, || יֵשַׁע‎ 45:8; 51:5, compare 42:21; צ ׳בשּׂר‎ Psa 40:10; צ ׳אִמְרַת‎ 119:123.

b. in name צִדְקֵנוּ יהוה‎, of Messianic king (vindicating people's cause and giving victory) Jer 23:6; of city 33:16.

c. of people as enjoying ׳צ‎ of salvation, || יְשׁוּעָה‎ Isa 62:1; || כָּבוֺד‎ 58:8; 62:2; צ יִלְבְּשׁוּ ׳כהנים‎ Psa 132:9; צ ׳שַׁעֲרֵי‎ 118:19; הצ ׳אֵילֵי‎ Isa 61:3.

d. of Cyrus, ׳צ לְרַגְלוֺ יִקְרָאֵהוּ‎ Isa 41:2 (who) in victory calleth him at every step (CheHpt on whose steps attends victory, so Di Du).

H6672. tsohar

I. [צֹ֫הַר‎] [noun masculine] only plural צָהֳרַ֫יִם‎ midday, noon, Deut 28:29+, צָהֳרָ֑יִם‎ Gen 43:16 +(when sun mounts its highest; on form as expanded plural (not dual) see Ges§ 88c and references); — usually

1 noon as a specific time of day, 1Kin 18:29; especially ׳בַּצּ‎ at noon Gen 43:16, 25; Amos 8:9; 1Kin 18:27; 20:16; Song 1:7 (resting-time for flock), Jer 6:4 (opposed to evening); צ ׳בְּעֵת‎ 20:16 (distinguished from morning) as time of supposed security 15:8; Zeph 2:4; also הַצּ וְעַד ׳מֵהַבֹּקֶר‎ 1Kin 18:26, ׳עַדהַֿצּ‎ 2Kin 4:20; without ב‎, as adverb, ׳צ‎ as time of prayer Psa 55:18 (+עֶרֶב בֹּקֶר,‎); as time of wasting קֶטֶב‎ 91:6; הַצּ ׳מִשְׁכַּב‎ 2Sam 4:5 noonday repose.

2 noon, as bright, simile of happiness, blessing, Isa 58:10 (opposed to אֲפֵלָה‎), Psa 37:6 (|| כָּאוֺר‎); compare Job 11:17 (Ges§ 133e); see also הַצּ ׳בְּתוֺךְ‎ Isa 16:3 (opposed to צִלֵּךְ‎); ׳בַּצּ‎ Deut 28:29; Isa 59:10; Job 5:14.

II. צֹ֫הַר‎ noun feminine probably roof (compare Arabic, Assyrian, Tel Amarna back; > Thes Di and others light, window); — לַתֵּבָה ׳צ תַּעֲשֶׂה‎ Gen 6:16.

צוה.def:
H6680. tsavah

[צָוָה‎]485 verb Pi`el lay charge (upon), give charge (to), charge, command, order (BaZMG xii (1887), 641 Gerber124op. Arabic combine, II. enjoin, IV. charge; injunction, command; Thes compare Syriac , heap up (stones), , stone-heap, Arabic guide-stone, compare Schulth57; Gerber makes Hebrew verbdenominative from מִצְוָה‎ but verb is much earlier); — Perfect3masculine singular צִוָּה‎ Gen 6:22 +; suffix צִוַּנִי‎ Deut 4:5 +; צִוְּךָ‎ 4:23 +; צִוָּהוּ‎ Gen 7:5 +, etc.; 1 singular צִוִּיתִי‎ Exod 29:35 29t., צִוֵּיתִי‎ Lev 8:31 4t., etc.; Imperfect3masculine singular יְצַוֶּה‎ Gen 18:19 8t.; יְצַו‎ Deut 28:8; וַיְצַו‎ Gen 2:16 +; suffix וִיצַוְּךָ‎ 1Chr 22:12, etc.; 1 Chronicles 1s. וָאֲצִוֶּה‎ Ezra 8:17 Qr (> Kt ואוצאה‎); 3 masculine plural וַיְצַזּוּ‎ Gen 50:16 +, etc.; Infinitive construct צַֹוּת‎ 2Sam 18:5 +, etc.; Imperative masculine singular צַוֵּה‎ Josh 4:16 + 2t.; צַו‎ Lev 6:2 9t.; masculine plural צַוּוּ‎ Josh 1:11; 4:3; Participle מְצַוֶּה‎ Num 32:23 +; construct מְצַוֵּה‎ Isa 55:4, etc.; feminine מְצַוָּה‎ Gen 27:8; —

1. a. lay charge upon, with עַל‎ person, Gen 2:16 (J) 28:6 (P) 1Kin 2:43; 11:11; Amos 2:12; Jer 35:6 + 6t.; עַל‎ of thing, מֵהַמְטִיר אֲצַוֶּה הֶעָבִים עַל‎ Isa 5:6, compare Job 36:32, ׳צ עַלתָֿגָב‎2Chr 7:13.

b. give charge to, command to with לְ‎ person Exod 1:22 (E) 1Sam 20:29; 1Chr 22:17; Isa 13:3; Jer 32:23; Psa 105:8 צ ׳תּוֺרָה משֶׁה לָנוּ‎ Deut 33:4, compare Neh 9:14; לְבֵיתֶ֑ךָ צַו‎ 2Kin 20:1 give charge to thy household (in preparation for death) = Isa 38:1 (compare Late Hebrew, B.Bath.151b, צַוָּאָה‎ 'verbal will' Id147a).

c. give charge uno, with אֶל‎ person Exod 16:34 (P), 1Kin 11:10; אֶלכֵּֿיתוֺ וַיְצַו‎ 2Sam 17:23 (compare

b.).

d. give charge over, appoint, with accusative of person + עַל‎ of thing, Neh 7:2; 1Chr 22:12, ׳צ עַל נָנִיד (לִהְיוֺת)‎ appoint one (to be) ruler over 2Sam 6:21; 1Kin 1:35; with לנגיד‎ 1Sam 13:14; 25:30; על שׁפטים‎ 2Sam 7:11 = 1Chr 17:10; with infinitive (no על‎), עמי לִרְעוֺת‎ 2Sam 7:7 = 1Chr 17:6; לְעֵינֵיהֶם אֹתוֺ וְצִוִּיתָה‎ Num 27:19 (P) and thou shalt install him in their sight, compare 27:23 (P).

e. give one charge, command (often עַל‎ concerning), Gen 12:20 (J), Num 8:22 (P), 2Sam 14:8; 18:5; Jer 7:22; 39:11; Isa 45:12 (AV RV Che RyKau; > Ges Ew Di Du and others as d), 10:6 (al. against), Nahum 1:14 (al. id.); with לְ‎ Num 9:8; 32:38 (P), Psa 91:11; Lam 1:17; Est 3:2; with אֶל‎ Isa 23:11; Jer 47:7.

2 charge, command:

a. with accusative of person + thing, often, especially of the law: Deuteronomic phrases are מצוךָ אנכי אשׁר‎ Exod 34:11 (J), Deut 4:40; 6:2, 6 18t. Deuteronomy, compare 15:15; אתכם מצוה אנכי אשׁר‎ 4:2 (twice in verse) + 9 t. Deuteronomy; צ ׳אשׁר הַדֶּרֶךְ‎ 13:6; 13:6; Exod 32:8 (E) Deut 5:30; 9:12, 16; 11:28; 31:29.

b. with accusative of person + object clause, e.g., Infinitive Gen 50:2+; ו‎ consecutive Perfect 18:19 (J), Num 35:2 (P); ו‎ consecutive Imperfect 2Sam 4:12; 1Kin 2:46; weak ו‎ with Imperfect Exod 27:20 (P) Josh 4:16; Imperative 1:9; 1Sam 18:22.

c. accusative of person, accusative of thing omitted, Exod 18:23 (E) Gen 49:33 (P) +; object given after לֵאמֹר‎ 26:11; 32:15, 20; Lev 6:2 +; וַיּאֹמֶר‎ etc., Gen 28:1; 49:29 +.

d. accusative of thing, accusative of person omitted, ׳צ בריתוֺ לעולם‎ Psa 111:9; צ ׳אֲשֶׁר ׳י הַדָּבָר וֶה‎, Exod 16:16, 32; 35:4; Lev 8:5; 9:6; 17:2; Num 30:2; 36:6 (P); object clause, Lev 8:34 (P), 13:54 (P); Gen 42:25 (E), 1 Kings 5:20; Judg 4:6.

e. absolute Gen 50:16 (E), Lam 3:37.

3 charge, command, accusative of person in phrase צ ׳כַּאֲשֶׁר‎ Exod 23:15 (E) Gen 7:9 (P) +; צ אשׁר ׳ככל‎ 7:5 (J) Exod 29:35 (P) +; צ ׳כאשׁר ׳י משֶׁה‎ 12:28, 50; 39:1, 5 37t. P; צ אשׁר ׳ככל ׳י משׁה‎ 39:32, 42 + 5t. צופי.def:
H853. eth

I. אֵת‎, with makk. אֶתֿ‎, with suffix אֹתִי‎; אֹתְכָה אֹתְךָ,‎ Num 22:33, אֹתָ֑כָה אֹתָ֑ךְ,‎ Exod 29:35, feminine אֹתָךְ‎; אֹתוֺ‎ etc.; 2 plural אֶתְכֶם‎, once אוֺתְכֶם‎ Josh 23:15; 3masculine plural regularly אֹתָם‎, rarely אֶתְהֶם‎ Gen 32:1; Exod 18:20; Num 21:3; Ezek 34:12; 1Chr 6:50, once אוֺתְהֶם‎ Ezek 23:45; 3feminine plural, on the contrary, regularly אֶתְהֶן‎ (13 t.), once אֹתָן‎ 16:54 (also אוֺתְהֶן‎ 23:47, אֹתָ֖נָה‎ Exod 35:26, אוֺתָ֖נָה‎ Ezek 34:21); forms with cholem also often written plene: — the

mark of the accusative, prefixed as a rule only to nouns that are definite (Moabite id., Phoenician אית‎ i.e. אִיַּת‎ (Schrödp. 213 f.); Aramaic יָת‎ frequently in ᵑ7‎; Syriac very rare as mark of accusative (for which is preferred), but used often in the sense of substance οὐσία, also in that of self, e.g. per se, reapse, sibi ipsi, PS1640f., Samaritan ; Arabic , only used with suffix, when it is desired to emphasize the pronoun, e.g. Qor 1:4 WAG i. § 189. [Ethiopic uses k£y¹ similarly, Di§ 150 a; but it is dubious if this is etymologically akin.] The primitive form will have been 'iwyath, originally a substantive with following Genitive, Olp. 432; whether ultimately a parallel development with אוֺת‎ sign from √ אוה‎ is uncertain: Ol WAG i. § 188 LagM i. 226 affirm, NöZMG 1886, 738 doubts. In Hebrew the ground-form is אוֺת‎; the forms with ¢, e being abbreviated. In post Biblical Hebrew, used in combination with another preposition: thus הַיּוֺם בְּאוֺתוֺ‎ = Bibl. הַשָּׁעָה בְּאוֺתָהּ הַהוּא, בַּיּוֺם‎; or as a nomin., e.g. הָאִישׁ אוֺתוֺ‎ = Bibl. הַהוּא הָאִישׁ‎).

1 As mark of the accusative prefixed to substantives defined either by the article (or כֹּל‎), or by a Genitive or pronominal affix, or in virtue of being proper names:

a. with transitive verbs, Gen 1:1, 16, 29, 30; 2:11; 4:1-2, 9:3 (אֶתֿכֹּל׃‎) etc. Similarly אֶתמִֿי‎ whom (in particular), Josh 24:15; 1Sam 12:3; 28:11; Isa 6:8 and elsewhere (but never אֶתמָֿה‎); also with זֶה‎ Gen 29:33; 44:29; 1 Samuel 21:16; 1Kin 22:27 +, זֹאת‎ Gen 29:27; 2Sam 13:27 +, אֵלֶּה‎ Gen 46:18; Lev 11:18; Isa 49:21 +. So pretty uniformly in prose; but in poetry את‎ is commonly dispensed with. By the use of את‎ with the pronominal affix, a pronoun can at once, if required, be placed in a position of emphasis; let the order of words from this point of view be carefully noticed in the following passages: Gen 7:1; 24:14; 37:4; Lev 10:17; 11:33; Num 22:32 thee I had slain, and her I had kept alive, Deut 4:14; 6:13, 23; 13:5; Judg 14:3 לִי קַח אוֺתָהּ‎ take for me her, 1Sam 14:35; 15:1; 18:17; 21:10 קָ֔ח תִּקַּחלְֿךָ אִםאֹֿתָהּ‎ if thou wilt take that, take it, 1Kin 1:35; 14:9; Isa 43:22; 57:11; Jer 9:2. So הַאוֺתִי‎ 5:22; 7:19. It also sometimes enables the reflexive sense to be expressed (elsewhere נַפְשָׁם‎) 7:19; Ezek 34:2. Rarely with a substantive which is undefined (Ew§ 277 d 2 Ges§ 117, 1, R. 2), as Exod 21:28; Num 21:9; Lev 20:14; 1Sam 24:6 (but see Dr) 2Sam 4:11; 18:18; 23:21; or which, though definite, is without the article, Gen 21:30; 2Sam 15:16; Lev 26:5; 1Sam 9:3 (so Num 16:15) Isa 33:19; 41:7; Ezek 43:10 (for further examples see Ew 1.c.)

b. with a passive verb (Ges§ 121. 1 Ew§ 295 b) conceived as expressing neutrally the action in question, and construed accordingly with an accusative of that which is its real object: examples occur with tolerable frequency from Gen 4:18 (J) אֶתעֿירָד לַחֲנוֺךְ וַיִּוָּלֵד‎, 17:5 (P), אַברָם אֶתשִֿׁמְךָ עוֺד יִקָּרֵא לֹא‎ there shall not be called (=one shall not call) thy name Abram, 21:5 (E), 27:42; 2Sam 21:11; 1Kin 18:13; Hosea 10:6 etc., to Jer 35:18; 38:4; 50:20; Ezek 16:4-5, Est 2:13 (compare DrJPh xi. 227 f.): also with passive verbs of filling (Ew§ 281 b), as Exod 1:7 +.

c. with neuter verbs or expressions, especially such as involve the idea of regarding, or treating, appy. by a construction κατὰ σύνεσιν (rare), Josh 22:17; 2Sam 11:25; Neh 9:32 (compare 1Sam 20:13 Dr). Once after אֵין‎, Hag 2:17; אֵלַיָֽ אֶתְכֶם אֵין‎.

d. poet. (si vera lectio), after an abstract noun used with a verbal force, Hab 3:13 (Amos 4:11; Isa 13:19; Jer 50:40 מַהְמֵּכָה‎ exerts a verbal force, like the Arabic nom. verbi [see WAG i. § 196, 43]; and Num 10:2; Ezek 17:9 לְמַשְׂאוֺת לְמַסַּע,‎ are Aramaizing infinitives: compare Ew§ 239 a).

2 את‎ marks an accusative in other relations than that of direct object to a verb: a. with verbs of motion (very rare) Num 13:17; Deut 1:19; 2:7 (to 'walk the wilderness'); denoting the goal Judg 19:18; Ezek 21:25 (Ew§ 281 d, n., 282 a 1). b. denoting time (duration), also very rare: Exod 13:7; Lev 25:22; Deut 9:25. c. expressing the accus. of limitation (rare): Gen 17:11, 14; 1Kin 15:23.

3 Chiefly in an inferior or later style, אֵת‎ (or וְאֵת‎) is used irregularly, partly (α), as it would seem, to give greater definiteness (so especially וְאֵת‎) at the mention of a new subject (when it may sometimes be rendered as regards), or through the influence of a neighbouring verb (a construct κατὰ σύνεσιν), or by an anacoluthon, partly (β) as resuming loosely some other preposition Thus (α) Exod 1:14; Num 3:26, 46; 5:10 (with הָיָה‎: so Ezek 35:10) Num 18:21b Deut 11:2 (anacoluthon), 14:13; Josh 17:11; Judg 20:44, 46 (contr. 20:25; 20:35) 1Sam 17:34 (see Dr) 26:16; 2Sam 21:22; 2Kin 6:5; Isa 53:8 (probably), 57:12; Jer 23:33 (but read rather with הַמַּשָּׂא אַתֶּם ᵑ9 ᵐ5‎) 27:8; 36:22; 38:16 Kt, 45:4 b Ezek 16:22; 17:21; 20:16; 29:4; b 43:7 (ᵐ5‎ Co prefix הֲרָאִיתָ‎) 44:3; Zech 8:17; Eccl 4:3; Dan 9:13; Neh 9:19, 34; 1Chr 2:9; 2Chr 31:17. In 1Sam 30:23; Hag 2:5 probably some such word as remember is to be understood. (β) Jer 38:9; Ezek 14:22; b 37:19 b Zech 12:10; אֵת סָבִיב‎ 1Kin 6:5; Ezek 43:17 strangely (in 1Kings ᵐ5‎ omits the clause: so StaZAW 1883, 135). — In 1Kin 11:1 וְ‎ is merely and also, and especially (see וְ‎); 11:25 is corrupt (read with הֲדָד עָשָׂה אֲשֶׁר הָרָעָה זֹאת ᵐ5‎); Ezek 47:17-18, 19 read similarly for זֹאת ואת,‎: see 47:20. — For some particulars as to the use of את‎, see A. M. WilsonHebraica. vi. 139 ff. 212 ff. (who, however, confuses it sometimes with II. אֵת‎). For denoting the pronominal object of a verb, את‎ with suffix preponderates relatively much above the verbal affix in P, as compared with J E Deuteronomy Judges Samuel Kings (see GieZAW 1881, 258 f.), — partly, probably, on account of the greater distinctness and precision which P loves.

יָת‎ mark of accusative (= Biblical Hebrew I. אֵת‎; Palmyrene ית‎; ZinjirliHad. 28 with suffix ותה‎; Nabataean, Palmyrene with suffix יתה‎ (Lzb263 Cooke170; compare RÉS468); ᵑ7‎ Samaritan יָת‎; Syriac (rare)); — Dan 3:12 יָָֽתְהוֺן מַנִּיתָ דִּי‎ whom thou hast appointed.

H3335. yatsar

יָצַר‎ verb form, fashion (Late Hebrew in participle יוֺצֵר‎ potter, creator, and derivatives; Phoenician יצר‎ potter; יצר ᵑ7‎ Syriac = יֵצֶר‎ etc.; Arabic covenant, contract; Assyrian êƒêru, as Hebrew, DlHWB 309) —

Qal Perfect ׳י‎ Isa 44:10; יָצָ֑ר‎ Gen 2:8; suffix יְצָרָהּ‎ Isa 45:18; 2masculine יָצַרְתָּ‎ Psa 104:26 8t. Perfect; Imperfect3masculine וַיִּ֫יצֶר‎ Gen 2:7; וַיִּ֫צֶר‎ 2:19; suffix יִצְּרֵהוּ‎ Isa 44:12; 1singular suffix אֶצֳּו֯רְךָ‎ Jer 1:5; Participle יוֺצֵר‎ Isa 41:25 20t.; יֹצֵר‎ 45:18 6t.; suffix יֹצְרִי‎ 49:5 11t. suffix; plural יוֺצְרִים‎ 30:14; 1Chr 4:23; construct יֹצְרֵי‎ Isa 44:9; —

H3426. yesh

יֵשׁ‎187 substantive being, substance, existence (on etymology see 2) — יֵשׁ‎ Gen 18:24 etc.; יֶשֿׁ‎ 31:29 + often; הֲיֵשׁ‎ 24:23 18t. (so אִשׁ‎ 2Sam 14:19 , הַאִשׁ‎ Micah 6:10 ), with suffix יֶשְׁךָ‎ Gen 24:42 2t.; יֶשְׁכֶם‎ 24:49 ; הֲיִשְׁכֶם‎ Deut 13:4 ; יֶשְׁנוֺ‎ (Ol§ 97 b Sta§ 370 b) 29:14; 1Sam 14:39 (+ 14:41 ᵐ5‎ We Dr), 23:23; Est 3:8 ; —

1 substance, only Prov 8:21 יֵשׁ אֹהֲבַי לְהַנְחִיל‎ to cause them that love me to inherit substance (so Sir 42:3).

2 elsewhere (properly as a substantive in the stative construct), it asserts existence, and so corresponds to the verb substantive, is (are, was, were, will be), literally the being, presence of... (so Biblical Aramaic אִתַי‎; Aramaic אית איתא,‎, [whence (self-) existent, essence, substance], with לָא‎ contracted לֵית לַיִת,‎, ; Mandean לאיית עית, עת,‎; Arabic [with irregular ] (inflected as a verb, , , etc.; WAG i. § 182, ii. § 42) is not ( is known only in two proverbial sayings, as a secondary form FlKl. Schr. i. 146 f.); Assyrian išû, be, have DlHWB 310; with affix 1 singular la-a i-ša-a-ku, I have not, TPi. 57 f.. On this word, see especially NöM. § 213, who exemplifies its different constructions in Semitic, and shews how it tends to pass into a verb; — (1) in Biblical Aramaic, Syriac, Babylonian ᵑ7‎, with possessive suffix; (2) in later Palestinian dialects, Jerusalem ᵑ7‎, Jerusalem Talmud, sometimes also in Babylonian ᵑ7‎ and Syriac, with independent personal pronoun (as הוא לית אנא, לית‎); (3) in Mandean, Babylonian Talmud, sometimes in Syriac and Arabic, and in Hebrew יֶשְׁנוֺ‎, with object. (verbal) suffix; (4) in Arabic, as a true verb. In Ethiopic literally therein, German es gibt, is similar in use (DiGr. § 167, l), though not of course in origin. In Hebrew the corresponding negative is אַיִן‎, q. v., the construction of which is quite similar) — is, are, was, were, etc., not, however, as a mere copula, but implying existence with emphasis (hence in English to be often represented by the substantive verb in italics):

a. with a predicate following, Gen 28:16 י ישׁ ׳אכן הזה במקום‎ surely Y. is (emphatic) in this place! 44:26 אִתְּכֶם אָחִינוּ יֵשׁ אִם‎; Exod 17:7 אַיִן אִם בְּקִרְבֵּנוּ יהוה הֲיֵשׁ‎, Num 22:29 בידי חרב ישׁ לו‎ Oh, that there were a sword in my hand! Deut 13:4 אֹהֲבִים הֲיִשְׁכֶם‎ whether you do love, 29:17 אישׁ בכם ישׁ פן‎, 29:18; 1Sam 9:11f. and they said, Is the seer here? and they said יֵשׁ‎ He is, 20:8; 23:23; Jer 27:18. Alone, in answer to a question (asked with יֵשׁ‎), He (it) is: 1Sam 9:12; 2Kin 10:15; Jer 37:17. But 23:26 (where ישׁ‎ has no substantive or suffix) text must be corrupt: compare Gie.

b. absolutely, there is (es. gibt, il y a), Gen 18:24 בעיר צדיקים חמשׁים ישׁ אולי‎ perhaps there are fifty righteous in the city, 24:23 ללון לנו מקום אביך בית הישׁ‎, 42:1 ׳במצ שׁבר ישׁ כי‎ that there was corn in Egypt, Judg 4:20 אישׁ פה הישׁ‎, 2Sam 9:1; 2Kin 5:8 he shall know that there is (emphatic) a prophet in Israel, Ruth 3:12 there is a kinsman nearer than I, Psalm 58:12 surely there are gods judging on the earth: so in aphorisms, asserting the existence of a particular character, quality, etc., Prov 11:24 עוד ונוסף מפזר ישׁ‎, 12:18; 13:7, 23; 14:12; 16:25; 18:24; 20:15; Eccl 2:21; 4:8; 5:12; 6:1, 11; 7:15 (twice in verse); 8:14 (3 t. in verse); 10:5. In questions, or protestations, יֵשׁ‎ often implies a doubt whether what is asked about is to be found or exists: 1Kin 18:10; Jer 5:1 and see אישׁ ישׁ אם‎ if there is (emphatic) a man doing justice, etc. (compare Psa 14:2), Psalm 14:22; Isa 44:8 אלהים הישׁ‎ is there a god beside me? Psa 7:4 בכפי עול ישׁ אם‎ if there is iniquity in my hands! 73:11 is there knowledge in the Most High? Job 5:1; 6:30; Lam 1:2.

c. special phrases: — (a) after אִם‎ and a participle, where an abiding intention is to be emphasized, Gen 24:42 דרכי מצליח אםיֿשׁךנֿא‎ if thou art (really), prospering my way, 24:49; 43:4; Judg 6:36 (compare II. אין‎

2b). (b) לְ יֵשׁ‎ = has (had), especially with pronouns לְךָ יֵשׁ לִי, יֵשׁ‎; etc., Gen 33:9 רָב יֶשׁלִֿי‎ I have plenty, 33:11; 43:7 אח לכם הישׁ‎, 44:20 זקן אב לנו ישׁ‎, 1Sam 17:40 that they may know לישׂראל אלהים ישׁ כי‎ that Israel has (emphatic) a god, 2Kin 4:2 מַהיֶּֿשׁלָֿכְי‎ what hast thou ? Job 14:7 for a tree has (emphatic) hope (compare Ruth 1:12), Ruth 25:3; Ruth 28:1; Ruth 38:28 אב למטר ׃הישׁ‎ Gen 39:5 (twice in verse); 39:8, * F f יֶשׁלֿו אשׁר כל‎ all that had (39:4 without אשׁר‎, probably error). (c) with infinitive and לְ‎, is it possible to... ? 2Kin 4:13; לדברלֿך הישׁ‎ can-1speak for thee to the king? 2Chr 25:9; so לְ אִשׁ‎ 2Sam 14:19 (compare לְ אֵין‎, below II. אַיִן‎

5). (d)... אֲשֶׁר יֵשׁ‎ (if) it was that... Num 9:20-21, there were some who... (with participle) Neh 5:2-3, 4 (compare Syriac for ὃ μὲν... ὃ δὲ ... Matt 13:8; PS172). (e) יָדִי יֶשׁלְֿאֵל‎ Gen 31:29 and elsewhere; see II. אֵל‎

7, p. 43. (f) 2Kin 10:15 וָיֵשׁ‎ and (if) it be... (compare וָלֹא‎ 5:17; 2Sam 13:26); so Judg 6:13 י ׳וְיֵשׁ אִתָּנוּ‎. (g) pleonastic יֵשׁ אֵין‎ Psa 135:17. (h) יֵשׁ לֹא‎ Job 9:33 (compare , : but ᵑ6 ᵐ5‎ Me and others לֻא‎). — As a rule, יֵשׁ‎ precedes its substantive (from which, however, like אין‎, it may be separated: Gen 24:23; 43:7 אָח לָכֶם הֲיֵשׁ‎, 44:19-20, 1Sam 20:8 etc.); but occasionally, for greater emphasis, this is prefixed: 21:5 ישׁ קדשׁ לחם אם כי‎ but holy bread there is! Isa 43:8 the blind people, ישׁ ועינים‎ though it has eyes, Judg 19:19 לי ישׁ ויין לחם‎ (compare אַיִן‎ 2c).

Bib.ACRE), ׳צ שָׂדֶה‎ 1Sam 14:14 (on text see Dr HPS); צִמְדֵּיכֶֿרֶם‎ Isa 5:10.

H6780. tsemach

צֶ֫מַח‎ noun masculineJer 23:5 sprout, growth; — absolute ׳צ‎ Hosea 8:7 +, צֶ֑מַח‎ Zech 3:8; construct צֶ֫מַח‎ Gen 19:25+; suffix צִמְחָהּ‎ Ezek 17:9 +; —

1 collective sprouting, growth, ׳צ הָאֲדָמָה‎ Gen 19:25 (J), ׳צ הַשָּׂדֶה‎ Ezek 16:7 (simile), compare Isa 61:11; Psa 65:11; so ׳צ יהוה‎ Isa 4:2, ׳צ‎ absolute Hosea 8:7; growth (= foliage) of vine, צ ׳טַרְמֵּי‎ Ezek 17:9.

צַמִּים‎ see צמם‎. צְמִיתֻת‎ see צמת‎. below,

צמם‎ (√ of following; compare Arabic draw together, or bandage (a wound),be compact; Late Hebrew צִמְצֵם‎ press; ᵑ7‎Jer Palpel, Ithpalpel veil (? denominative)).

צַמִּים‎ noun masculine doubtful word, usually snare, trap (from || מַּח‎ Job 18:9); — צ ׳וְשָׁאַף חֵילָם‎ 5:5 and a snare snappeth at his wealth (so Bu BevJphil. xxvi. 304 f.; Vrss Di Du and most modern צְמֵאִים‎, or צָמֵא‎, the thirsty, sometiems with change ofוְשָׁאַף‎); 18:9 (|| מַּח‎; CheJq ix (1897), 578 צִירִים‎ pangs, compare Isa 13:8).

Qal Participle active plural צֹמְקִים שָׁדַיִם‎ Hosea 9:14 shrivelling breasts (of women; || מַשְׁכִּיל רֶחֶם‎).

Qal, Pi`el) hyperbolic (properly compress, Late Hebrew id., press together; Arabic is be silent, II, IV.make speechless, silence; Syriac be silent (in Lexicons)); —

צניפה.def:

צָנִיף‎ noun masculineZech 3:5 turban; — absolute ׳צ‎ 3:5 (twice in verse) (for high priest) and (figurative of righteousness) Job 29:14; construct מְלוּכָה צְנִיף‎ Isa 62:3 Qr royal turban (Kt צנוף‎); plural הַצְּנִיפוֺת‎ 3:23 (of women's turbans).

צנם.def:
H6798. tsanam

[צָנַם‎] verb dry up, harden (compare Aramaic צוּנָּמָא‎,, stone); —

I. צנן‎ (√ of following; meaning obscure).

צנע.def:
H6800. tsana

[צָנַע‎] verb be modest, humble (perhaps properly be retired, Late Hebrew Hiph`il keep close, reserve, preserve, so אַצְנַע ᵑ7‎; צְנִיעַ‎ retiring, modest); —

Hiph`il Infinitive absolute לֶכֶת הַצְנֵעַ‎ Micah 6:8 a making humble to walk = shewing a humble walk (with God).

[צָנוּעַ‎]

adjective modest (on formation compare BaBN § 31 d); — plural צְנוּעִים‎ Prov 11:9 (see Toy; opposed to זָדוֺן‎).

צנף.def:
H6801. tsanaph

[צָנַף‎] verb wrap, or wind up, together (compare Arabic hem of garment, ᵑ7‎J צְנָפָא‎ skirt ( = כָּנָף‎); מַצְנֵפָא‎ turban, Christian-Palestinian Aramaic tassel); —

Qal Imperfect3masculine singular יִצְנֹף‎ Lev 16:4 he shall wind (his head) with (ב‎) the turban ( מִצְנֶפֶת‎ q. v.); suffix, + Infinitive absolute and accusative of congnate meaning with verb צְנֵפָה יִצְנָפְךָ צָנוֺף‎ Isa 22:18 he will wind thee entirely up (with) a winding (under figure of ball, to be driven far off, in exile). — צנוף‎ 62:3 see following.

צנפה.def:
H6802. tsenephah

צְנֵפָה‎ noun feminine winding; — Isa 22:18, see [צנף‎].

צנצנת.def:
H6803. tsintseneth

צִנְצֶ֫נֶת‎ noun feminine jar, or like receptacle (so vrss and context; perhaps from above v; > basket = ᵑ7‎ Talmud צִנָּא‎); — Exod 16:33 (P).

צְנָן‎ see צַאֲנָן‎ .

צנתרות.def:
H6804. tsanteroth

צַנְתְּרוֺת‎ noun masculine plural construct pipes feeding lamps with oil Zech 4:12 (in vision) (formation by inserting ת‎ according to Bö§ 300 b Köii.1.201).

צעד.def:
H6806. tsaad

[צַ֫עַד‎] noun masculine2Sam 6:13 step, pace; — absolute צָ֑עַד‎ Prov 30:29; suffixצַעֲדוֺ‎ Jer 10:3; Prov 6:9, etc.; plural construct צַעֲדֵי‎ Job 18:7; suffix צְעָדַי‎ 31:4, etc.; —

1 literally step, pace, 2Sam 6:13, תַּחְתֵּנִי צַעֲדִי תַּרְחִיב‎ 22:37 = Psa 18:37, i.e. givest me firm footing, צ ׳מֵטִיבֵי‎ Prov 30:29 = making a good step, stately in march; Lam 4:18 (|| לָ֑כֶת‎).

2 step, steps, in figure of course of life, fortune: singular צ יֵצַר ׳לֹא‎ Prov 4:12; || דֶּרֶךְ‎ Jer 10:23; Prov 16:9; Job 14:16; 31:4; 34:21, אוֺנוֺ צַעֲדֵי‎ 18:7 (compare Prov 4:12 above); אַגִּידֶנּוּ מִסְמַּרעָֿדַי‎ Proverbs 31:37; of harlot 5:5 figurative, יִתְמֹ֑כוּ צְעָדֶיהָ שְׁאוֺל‎.

צעדה.def:
H6807. ts

'adah I. צְעָדָה‎ noun feminine marching; — צ ׳קוֺל‎ 2Sam 5:24 the sound of marching = 1Chr 14:15.

II. [צְעָדָה‎] noun feminine armlet, band clasping upper arm (so SS and others; most step-chain, from I. צעד‎); — plural הַצְּעָדוֺת‎ Isa 3:20 (ladies' finery); read ׳הַצּ‎ also 2Kin 11:12 (for הָעֵדוּת ᵑ0‎) WeBi. Eini. 4, 258 = compare (2), 361 Kmp SS Kit Benz.

צעה.def:
H6808. tsaah

[צָעָה‎] verb stoop, bend, incline (Arabic (, ) incline, lean, compare also ); —

Qal Participle

1 צֹעֶה‎ Isa 51:14 one stooping (under a burden), 63:1 bending (forward or backward; from abundant strength), but read probably צֹעֵד‎ marching (Lo Gr Che Du Di-Kit and others); feminine זֹּנָה צֹעָה אַתְּ‎ Jer 2:20 (in sensu obscoeno).

2 transitive (=

Pi`el q. v.) plural צֹעִים‎ Jer 48:12 men inclining, tipping a vessel, to empty it.

Pi`el Perfect3plural suffix וְצֵעֻהוּ‎ Jer 48:12 I will send tippers and they shall tip him over (Moab, under figure of vessel).

צעיף.def:
H6809. tsaiph

צָעִיף‎ noun [masculine] wrapper, shawl, or veil; — absolute ׳צ‎ Gen 24:65; 38:14; suffix צְעִיפָהּ‎ 38:19 (all J).

צַעֲצֻעִים‎ see צוע‎.

צעיר.def:
H6810. tsair

I. צָעִיר‎ adjective little, insignificant, young; — absoluteצָעִיר‎ Gen 25:23 +; feminine צְעִירָה‎ 19:31 +; צְעִרָה‎ 1Sam 9:12; masculine plural צְעִירִים‎ Job 30:1; suffix צְעִירֶיהָ‎ Jer 48:4 Qr (Kt צעוריה‎ but see צֹעַר‎); צְעִירֵיהֶם‎ 14:3 (Kt צעוריהם‎), etc.; —

1.a. little, with idea of insignificance Judg 6:15 (|| הַדַּל‎), compare 1Sam 9:21 (|| קְטַנֵּי‎), Micah 5:1; Psa 68:28; Isa 60:22 (opposed to עצום גוי‎); of horn in vision Dan 8:9, read probablyצעירה אחרת‎ for מִצְּעִירָה אחת‎, compare Bev Dr; הַצֹּאן צְעִירֵי‎ Jer 49:20; 50:45 (figurative of helpless captives).

b. insignificant, mean, Psa 119:141 (|| נִבְזֶה‎), Jer 14:3 (as substantive); on 48:4.see צֹעַר‎.

2 more often of age, young (usually with article the younger, youngest, as substantive), of son (brother), opposed to הַבְּכוֺר‎ Gen 43:33; 48:14 (both J), Josh 6:26; 1Kin 16:34, opposed to רַב‎ Gen 25:23 (J), compare יְשִׁישִׁים ואתם לְיָמִים ׳צ אני‎ Job 32:6; of daughter (sister), opposed to הַבְּכִירָה‎ Gen 19:31, 34, 35, 38(J) 29:26 (E); — here belongs also לימים מִמֶּנִּי צְעַירִים‎ Job 30:1, si vera lectio; GHBWr Siegf Bu strike out לימים ממני‎; ᵐ5‎ ἐλἁχιστοι); put then under 1b.

צעירה.def:
H6812. tseirah

[צְעִירָה‎] noun feminine youth; — suffix כִּצְעִרָתוֺ‎ Gen 43:33 (J; opposed to כִּבְכֹרָתוֺ‎). — On adjective צְעִירָה‎ see foregoing; צעוריה‎ Jer 48:4 צעוריהם‎ 14:3, see צָעִיר צֹעַר,‎.

צען.def:
H6813. tsaan

[צָעַן‎] verb wander, travel (Arabic journey, go away; probably connected with Assyrian ƒênu, Ethiopic , Aramaic טְעַן‎, Palmyrene טען‎, all load (beast, etc.) = Hebrew טָעַן‎ Gen 45:17; Aramaic טְעַן‎, also bear, carry); —

Qal Imperfect3masculine singular יִצְעָן‎ Isa 33:20 travel, i. e. be removed, of tent (+ יִסַּע‎).

צעננים.def:
H6815. Tsaanannim

צַעֲנַנִּים‎ proper name, of a location only with בְּ‎, pointed as preposition, and so most (but ב‎ perhaps radical, see GFM); on border of Naphtali, near Kedesh; — ׳בְּצ‎ Josh 19:33 (Βεσεμεειν, Σεενανειμ, etc.) + Judg 4:11 Qr (Kt בצענים‎), ᵐ5‎ πλεονεκτούντων (√ בָּצַע‎), ἀναπαυομένων.

צעף‎ (√ of following; compare Arabic III. make double, double; Ethiopic fold, double, so Aramaic עוּף‎, , double (for = צָעִיף‎), compare עֵיפָא ᵑ7‎ for Hebrew צָעִיף‎ (properly a double or folded thing); see especially Lagsem.i.23.f f.).

צעצעים.def:
H6816. tsaatsuim

צַעֲצֻעִים‎ noun [masculine] plural things formed, images; צ ׳מַעֲשֵׂה‎2Chr 3:10 image work (of cherubim).

צעק.def:
H6817. tsaaq

צָעַק‎ verb cry, cry out, call (|| זָעַק‎; Late Hebrew id.; Arabic perhaps originally sound as thunder, compare thunderbolt, bellow (of bull)); —

Qal Perfect3masculine singular׳צ‎ 1Kin 20:39; Lam 2:18, 3feminine singular צָֽעֲקָה‎ Deut 22:24 +, etc.; Imperfect יִצְעַק‎ Exod 23:22 +, etc.; Imperative feminine singular וְצַעֲקִי‎ Jer 22:20, וּצֳעָ֑קִי‎ 22:20; feminine plural צְעַקְנָה‎ 49:3; Infinitive absolute צָעֹק‎ Exod 22:22; construct לִצְעֹק‎ 2Kin 8:3; Participle feminine singular absolute צֹעֶ֫קֶת‎ 8:5; masculine plural צֹעֲקִים‎ Gen 4:10; Exod 5:8; —

1 cry, cry out, for help, usually with אֶל‎ person; —

a. unto man Gen 41:55 (E; + ל‎ of thing), Num 11:3 (JE), 1Kin 20:39; 2Kin 6:26; 8:3 (+ אֶל‎ of thing), 8:5 (+ עַל‎ of thing); followed by אמר‎ Exod 5:15 (J), 2Kin 4:1 and (אֶל‎ person omitted) Exod 5:8 (J), 2Kin 4:40; 6:5.

b. especially unto ׳י‎: Gen 4:10; Exod 8:8 ( + דְּבַר עַלֿ‎ of thing), 14:10, 15; 15:25; 17:4; 22:22 (יִצְעַק צָעֹק‎), 22:26; Num 12:13; 20:16; Josh 24:7 (all J E), Judg 4:3; 10:12; Deut 26:7; Isa 19:20 (+ מִמְּנֵי‎ of thing), Lam 2:18; Neh 9:27; Psa 107:6; 107:28; ׳אֶלאֿ וְאֶצְעָ֑קָה קוֺלִי‎ 77:2, compare 34:18; with ׳לי‎2Chr 13:14: נֶגְדֶּ֑ךָ‎ Psa 88:2.

c. cry unto (אֶל‎) idol Isa 46:7.

2 absolute cry, cry out, in distress, need; — Gen 27:34 (J; with accusative of congnate meaning with verb), Deut 22:24, 27; Isa 33:7 (|| בָּכָה‎), 65:14 (|| הֵילִיל‎, opposed to רָנַן‎; with מִן‎ of thing), Jer 22:20 (twice in verse) (|| קוֺל נָתַן‎), 49:3 (|| הֵילִיל‎), Job 35:12; with object חָמָס‎ 19:7 (|| אֲשַׁוַּע‎).

3 make outcry, clamour, Isa 42:2 (+ קוֺלוֺ יַשְׁמִיעַ יִשָּׂא,‎ ).

Niph`al be summoned (i.e. to arms), absolute; Imperfect3masculine singular וַיִּצָּעֵק‎ Judg 7:23-24, 12:1, Songs 3 masculine plural וַיִּצָּֽעֲקוּ‎ 10:17; 2Kin 3:21, followed by שָׁאוּל אַחֲרֵי‎ + accusative of location 1Sam 13:4.

Pi`el Participle מְצַעֵק‎ cry aloud, in grief, 2Kin 2:12.

Hiph`il call together אֶליֿ ׳וַיַּצְעֵקאֶתהָֿעָם הַמִּצְמָּה‎ 1Sam 10:17.

צעקה.def:
H6818. tseaqah

צְעָקָה‎ noun feminine cry, outcry (older form of זְּעָקָה‎); — absolute׳צ‎ Gen 27:34 +; construct צַעֲקַת‎ Exod 3:9 +; suffix צַעֲקָתוֺ‎ 1Sam 9:16 +, etc.; —

1 outcry against (Sodom) Gen 18:21; 19:13 (both J).

2 cry of distress especially as heard by ׳י‎ Exod 3:7 (J), 22:22 (E), compare Isa 5:7; Job 27:9; 34:28; Psa 9:13; ׳צ אֵלַי בָּאָה‎ Exod 3:9 (E), 1Sam 9:16, compare Job 34:28; ׳צ גְּדֹלָה‎ Exod 11:6; 12:30 (both J), Neh 5:1; as accusative of congnate meaning with verb Gen 27:34 (J); צ ׳קוֺל‎ 1Sam 4:14; Jer 25:36 (|| יְלָלָה‎), Zeph 1:10 (|| id., + גדול שֶׁבֶר‎), Jer 48:3 (|| גדול וָשֶׁבֶר שֹׁד‎), compare 49:21; שֶׁבֶר צַעֲקַת‎ 48:5; (|| בְּכִי‎).

צער.def:
H6819. tsaar

[צָעַר‎] verb be, or grow, insignificant (|| זער‎; Late Hebrew id., Assyrian ƒe—êru, be small, Arabic id.; Syriac be insignificant, despicable; צְעַר ᵑ7‎ transitivedespise, revile; —

Qal Imperfect (opposed to כָּבֵד‎), 3 masculine plural יִצְעֲרוּ‎ Job 14:21, יִצְעָ֑רוּ‎ Jer 30:19; Participle as substantive הַצֹּעֲרִים‎ Zech 13:7 (i.e. sheep, in figure, compare Now).

צפד.def:
H6821. tsaphad

צָפַד‎ verb draw together, contract (Late Hebrew id., trams; Arabic bind fast, shackle, compare NöM § 46 who compare Mand סאפטים‎ fetters); —

Qal Perfect3masculine singular ׳צ‎ Lam 4:8 their skin contracteth, shrivelleth, upon (עֵל‎) their bones.

צָפָה‎ Ezek 32:6 see צוף‎

צפה.def:
H6824. tsaphah

[צָפָה‎] noun feminine out-flow; — suffix צָפָֽתְךָ‎ Ezek 32:6 thine outflow (flowing blood), Co Bthl Toy Krae.

צוֺפַי‎ = II. צוּף‎. צוֺפִים‎ see צוּפִי‎. above

H6825. Tsepho

or Tsephi צְפִי צְפוֺ,‎ proper name, masculine Σωφαρ: in Edom (? gaze, gazing); — צְפוֺ‎ Gen 36:11, 15 + 36:43 (insert probably after עירם‎; compare LagSept. Stud. ii.10.1. 178; 37, 1. 270 NesMar.12) = צְפִי‎ 1Chr 1:36.

H6826. tsippuy

צִמּוּי‎ noun [masculine] metal plating; — of idols Isa 30:22, capitals Exod 38:17, 19, altar Num 17:3; 17:4.

צפון.def:
H6828. tsaphon

I. צָפוֺן‎153 noun feminineIsa 43:6 north (as the hidden, dark; compare Thes LewyFremdw. 188 f.; perhaps Phoenician צפל‎ north); — absolute ׳צ‎ Jeremiah 26:26 +, צָפֹ֫נָה‎ northward Gen 13:14 +, oftener צָפ֫וֺנָה‎ Jer 3:12 +, also צָפ֫וֺנָה‎ = צָפוֺן‎ 1:13 + (after prepositions and stative construct; compare Ges§ 90e); construct לְ מִצְּפוֺן‎ Josh 8:11 +, also מִצְּפוֺן‎ 19:14 Gi (compare Benn; van d. H. Baer ׳מִצָּ‎), לְ מִצְּפ֫וֺנָה‎ Judg 21:19; (׳צ‎ occurs oftenest in Ezekiel [46 t.], Joshua [25 t.], Jeremiah [25 t.], Daniel [9 t.]); — north (opposite south, east, west) Gen 13:14; 28:14 (both J), Exod 27:11 (P), +; צ ׳מְּאַת‎ north side 26:20; Josh 15:5 + (see מֵּאָה‎); so צ ׳צֶלַיע‎ Exod 26:35, הַצּ ׳רוּחַ‎ Ezek 42:17, compare צָפ֫וֺנָה הַמִּזְבֵּחַ עַליֶֿרֶךְ‎ 2Kin 16:14; צ ׳גְּבוּל‎ Num 34:7, 9 north boundary; צ ׳יַתְכְּתֵי‎ remote parts of north Isa 14:13 (as divine abode), Ezek 38:6, 15 + (see [ יַרְכָה‎]); הַצּ ׳שַׁעַר‎ 40:35 +, צ ׳מֶּתַח‎ 42:2; צ ׳רוּחַ‎ Ezekiel 25:23 north wind, and so ׳צ‎ alone Song 4:16; toward the north is צָפ֫וֺנָה‎ Josh 13:3 +?אֶלצָֿפוֺן‎ Eccl 1:6, ׳אֶלהַֿצּ‎ Ezek 42:1, אֶלהַֿצָּפ֫וֺנָה‎ 8:14, לַצָּפוֺן‎ 40:23, הַצָּפוֺן דֶּרֶךְ‎ 40:20, ׳ד צָפ֫וֺנָה‎ 8:5 (twice in verse) +, etc.; especially (in Jeremiah, Ezekiel, etc.) of quarter whence invaders were to come, e. g. Assyrians Isa 14:31, compare Zeph 2:13, Babylonians Jer 6:1, 22; 15:12; 46:20, 24 (׳עַםצֿ‎), 47:2, Ezek 26:7, Cyrus against Babylonian Isa 41:25, compare Jer 50:3, 9, 41; 51:48; more vaguely, 1:14-15, (צ ׳מַמְלְכוֺת‎), 4:6; 10:22; 13:20; 25:9, 26 (הַצּ ׳מַלְכֵי‎); of Gog's host Ezek 38:6, 15; 39:2; צ ׳נְסִיכֵי‎ 32:30 (apparently of nearer [Aramaean?] princes); צ ׳אֶרֶץ‎ Jer 31:8 is region of Carchemish, but Zech 2:10; 6:6, 8 (twice in verse) of Babylon; צ ׳מֵאֶרֶץ‎ (sometimes + other countries) the exiles and dispersed are to return Jer 3:18; 16:15 = 23:8; 31:8, compare Isa 43:6; 49:12; הַצּ ׳מֶלֶךְ‎ Dan 11:6-7, 8, 11, 13, 15, 40 denotes successive Seleucidae.

צפוני.def:
H6831. Tsephoni

I. צְפוֺנִי‎ adjective, of a people of צְפוֺן‎ (see foregoing); with articleas substantive collective Num 26:15. — II.׳צ‎ see צפן‎.

צפור.def:
H6833. tsippor

I. צִמֹּר צִמּוֺר,‎40

noun feminineAmos 3:5 (masculine Psa 102:8, compare KöSynt § 252 a, so 104:17, yet compare AlbrZAW xvi (1896). 71), bird; — absolute צִמּוֺר‎ Hosea 11:11 15t., צִמֹּר‎ Gen 15:10-11t., construct צִמּוֺר‎ Deut 4:17 5t., צִמֹּרֹ‎ Psa 8:9; plural צִמְָּרִים‎ Lev 14:4-5t.; —

1 single bird, Amos 3:5; Hosea 11:11 (simile; || יוֺנָה‎), Lam 3:52; Job 40:29; Psa 102:8; 124:7; Prov 6:5; 7:23; 26:2; 27:8 (all simile), Lev 14:5 10t. Leviticus 14; כָּלצֿ ׳בָּנָף‎ Deut 4:17, ׳כָּלצֿ טְהוֺרָה‎ 14:11 (כל‎ distributive); ׳קַןצֿ‎ 22:6 bird's nest, הַצּ ׳קוֺל‎ Eccl 12:4; plural Isa 31:5 (simile), Neh 5:18; Lev 14:4 (צִמְָּרִים שְׁתֵּי‎, in purify.; compare WeHeid. 2.171 RSSemitic i. 402, 2nd ed. 422), 14:49 (id.), Psa 104:17; Eccl 9:12.

2 less often collective, either def. Gen 15:10 (two), or indefinite Psa 11:1 (figurative), שָׁמַיִם צִמֹּר‎ 8:9, especially ׳צ כָּלכָּֿ֠נָף‎ Ezek 39:17; Psa 148:10, צ ׳כֹּל כָּלכָּֿנָף‎ Psalm 17:23; Gen 7:14, also redund. with צ ׳עֵיט כָּלכָּֿנָף עַיִט,‎ Ezek 39:4 birds of prey of all kinds.

[צִמַּר‎] noun feminineDan 4:18 (compare Kp. 165, Anm. 3) bird (see Biblical Hebrew II. צפר‎); — plural absolute צִמֲּרִין‎ 4:30, emphatic צִמְּרַיָּא‎ 4:11, construct צִמֲּרֵי‎) 4:9; 4:18.
