צפתה.def:
ו‎

ו‎, Waw, sixth letter; in modern Hebrew = numeral 6; no evidence of this usage in OT times.

וָ וּ, וְ,‎

demonstrative adverb and

conjunction so, then, and (Phoenician, Moabite, Aramaic ו‎; Arabic ; Ethiopic Assyrian u DlW (but between verbs the usually connective is the enclitic ma KAT2. 508, Dl§§ 82, 150). The use in Hebrew shews that original וְ‎ was not a merely copulative conjunction, but that it possessed a demonstrative force (compare Dr§ 122), which is often perceptible as such, though in other cases, from its being applied to denote mere juxtaposition or connection [compare Greek τε, and Latin tum .... tum = 'both .... and,' both properly demonstratives: Assyrian ma has also a demonstrative force, Dl§ 79], it is less palpable) — וְ‎ before shwa' mobile or a labial is vocalized וּ‎; often before a tone-syll., when the word itself has a disj. accent, וָ‎ (as וַָמתִּי׃‎ Gen 19:19; וָמֵ֖תוּ‎ 33:13; וָמֵ֑ת‎ 44:9; וָחָֽיָה׃‎ Exod 1:16; וָיָ֑מָּה‎ Josh 15:46; וָ֔לֹ֕א‎ 2Sam 13:26; וָאָ֖רֶץ‎ Isa 26:19; וָקָ֔מוּ‎ 49:7; וָחָֽתָּה׃‎ Jer 48:1; וָרָֹע‎ Psa 10:15); especially when it forms with the preceding word a pair, whether of parallel or opposed ideas (as וָכֹה כֹּה‎ Exod 2:12, וָמִ֖י מִי‎ 10:8, וָאָ֑בֶן אֶבֶן‎ Deut 25:13; וָדֹ֑ר דֹּר‎ 32:7 +; וָבֹ֔הוּ תֹּהוּ‎ Gen 1:2, וָרֶמֶ֛שׂ בְּהֵמָה‎ 1:24, וָרָֽע׃ טוֺב‎ 2:19, וָנָ֖ד נָע‎ 4:12, וָלָ֖יְלָה וְיוֺם וָחֹ֛רֶף וְקַיִץ‎ 8:22, וֵָלךְ׃ קַח‎ 12:19, וָאָֽרֶץ׃ שָׁמַיִם‎ 14:19, וָאָ֑תָּה אֲנִי‎ 31:44, וָה֑וּא אֲנִי‎ 41:11, וָשׁוּבוּ עִבְרוּ‎ Exod 32:27, וָהֵ֛ם אַתָּה‎ Num 16:16, וָמֶ֑לָךְ אֱלֹהִים‎ 1Kin 21:13, וָנֶ֖כֶד נִין‎ Isa 14:22, וָשֶׁ֖בֶר שֹׁד‎ 59:7; and often: see more fully Bö§ 600); occasionally also with a conjunctive accent (as לְעֹלָֽם׃ וָשַחי‎ Gen 3:22 compare Lev 18:5, שָׁם וָמַ֣תְנוּ‎ 2Kin 7:4, חֲדָשָׁ֑ה וָאָ֣רֶץ‎ Isa 65:17; Prov 25:3, גָּדוֺל׃ וָשֶשׁבֶר שֹׁ֖ד‎ Jer 48:3, compare 32:29). — וְ‎ is used very freely and widely in Hebrew, but also with much delicacy, to express relations and shades of meaning which Western languages would usually indicate by distinct particles. But in Hebrew particles such as לָכֵן לְמַעַן, בַּעֲבוּר, אוּלָם, אָכֵן, אַךְ, אָז, אוֺ,‎, etc., were reserved for cases in which special emphasis or distinctness was desired: their frequent use was felt instinctively to be inconsistent with the lightness and grace of movement which the Hebrew ear loved; and thus in AV, RV, words like or, then, but, notwithstanding, howbeit, so, thus, therefore, that, constantly appear, where the Hebrew has simply וְ‎.

1 And, connecting both words (see above), and sentences (Gen 1:5 וג קָרָא ׳וְלַחשֶׁךְ‎). When three, four, or more words follow, the conjunction may connect them all, as 7:21; 10:2 (6 t.) 24:35 (7 t.) Josh 7:24 (10 t.) 2Sam 17:28f.: often however it is prefixed only to the last, as Gen 5:32; 10:1; Deut 18:10 etc.; occas. even it connects only the first two, 1Kin 8:47; Isa 1:13; Psa 45:9; Job 42:9. Remarkably, however, וְ‎ as a mere conjunction is, as a rule, not in classical Hebrew attached directly to verbs (especially in the perfect), the construction with וְ‎ consecutive (see

2) being (as in Moabite) preferred: thus וַיִּבֶן יָצָא‎ is said, not וּבָנָה יָצָא‎. Exceptions in classical Hebrew are (a) sometimes where synonyms are coupled, as Num 23:19 וְדִבֶּר ֗֗֗ אָמַר‎, Deut 2:30; Judg 5:26; 1Sam 12:2; Isa 1:2 ורוממתי גדּלתי‎ 2:11; 5:14; 8:8; 19:6; 29:20; (b) isolated cases, difficult to reduce to rule (perhaps sometimes due to textual error), as Gen 28:6; 38:5; Judg 3:23; 7:13; 16:18; 1Sam 1:12; 3:13; 4:19; 5:7; 10:9; 17:38, 48; 25:20 and elsewhere (in other passages, apparently similar, the perfect and וְ‎ has a frequent. force (see 2), as Gen 37:3; Exod 36:29f.; Num 10:17f. 21:15, 20; 1Sam 2:22; 16:14; 17:34f. (see Dr) 27:9; 2Sam 16:13; 17:17, perhaps also Gen 15:6; 21:25; 34:5). In later parts of OT, probably through Aramaic influence, the perfect with simple וְ‎ occurs more frequently: so especially in Ecclesiastes, where it is all but universal (e.g. 2:11-12, 13, 15 etc.). With the imperfect, the simple וְ‎ is not so unidiomatic, even in classical Hebrew (compare 3); see 1:9, 26; 9:27; 17:2; 22:17; 27:29; Exod 23:8 (frequently) 24:7; Num 14:12; Deut 17:13; 30:12-13, Josh 3:13; 7:3; Judg 7:3; 13:8; Isa 5:29; 14:10; often also in Jeremiah, Isa2, Job, Psalms, e.g. 40:30; 41:20 (Dr§ 116: contrast 28:13). See more fully Dr§ 130-4 Ges§ 112. 6. Special senses: —

a. it sometimes = and specially, Gen 3:16; 1Kin 11:1 many strange women, and specially the daughter of Pharaoh, Isa 1:1 Judah and (= and particularly) Jerusalem, 2:1; 9:7; Psa 18:1.

b. and in particular ('und zwar'), and that (explicative), Gen 4:4; Judg 7:22; 1Sam 17:40 וּבַיַּלְקוּט‎, 28:3 in Ramah, and that in his city (unusual: text suspicious), 2Sam 13:20 וְשֹׁמֵמָה‎ and that desolate, Isa 57:11 I have been silent וּמֵעוֺלָם‎ and that from of old, 32:7; Jer 15:13; Amos 3:11 (si vera lectio), 4:10; Zech 9:9b Mal 1:11; Psa 68:10; Prov 3:12; Lam 3:26; Eccl 8:2; Dan 1:3; 8:10; 9:25, 27; Neh 8:13; 1Chr 9:27; 2Chr 8:13; 29:27 (but' even' for ו‎, before ל‎ and infinitive, e.g. in Isa 44:28; Jer 17:10; 19:12, is wrong; see Ew§ 351 c, Dr§ 206).

c. sometimes it introduces an idea which so exceeds or adds to what has preceded, that it is nearly equivalent to also, 1Sam 25:43; 1Kin 2:22 ask also the kingdom for him; unusually Hosea 8:6 והוא מישׂראל כי‎ for of Israel is it also, Eccl 5:6 והבלים‎ (see De) 2Chr 27:5 (but see ᵐ5‎). Or it may be rendered yea: so especially in the ascending numerations 3-4 Amos 1:3, 6, 9, 11, 13; 2:1, 4, 6; Prov 30:18, 21, 29, 6-7 6:16; Job 5:19, 7-8 Micah 5:4 — the first number being aggravated, or augmented, by a higher. In one idiom וּגְבוּל‎, occurring in geographic descriptions, it is used peculiarly, seemingly = at the same time: Num 34:6 and as for the western border, וּגְבוּל הַגָּדוֺל הַיָּם לָכֶם וְהָיָה‎ the great sea shall be to you also (German 'zugleich') a border, Deut 3:16 וּגְבוּל הַנַּחַל תּוֺךְ‎ the middle of the stream being at the same time the border, 3:17; Josh 13:23, 27; 15:12, 47 (but these, except Num 34:6, might be cases of 5c γ).

d. it connects alternative cases, so that it = or: Exod 20:10, 17; 21:16 he that stealeth a man בְיָדוֺ וְנִמְצָא וּמְכָרוֺ‎ and selleth him, and (= or if) he be found in his hand, 21:17; Lev 21:14; 22:23-24, Prov 29:9 (Fl Ew RV: whether . . . or) Job 31:13, 16, 26, etc.

e. it connects contrasted ideas, where in our idiom the contrast would be expressed explicitly by but; in such cases prominence is usually given to the contrasted idea by its being placed immediately after the conjunction: Gen 2:17 but of the tree of the knowledge . . . thou shalt not eat, 4:2, 5; 6:8; 17:21; 31:10 etc., 1Kin 2:26; 10:7; 11:32, 34; 15:14; Prov 10:1-2, 3, 4 + often; even after לֹא‎ (where כִּי‎ or אִם כִּי‎ might be expected), as Gen 42:10; Exod 21:18; Lev 26:45; Deut 11:11; Judg 19:12; 1Kin 3:11.

f. it introduces a contrasted idea in such a way as to suggest a question, especially before a pronoun, Judg 14:16 I told it not to my father or my mother, אַגִּיד וְלָךְ‎ and shall I told it unto thee? 2Sam 11:11; Jer 25:29 תִנָּקוּ הִנָּקֵה וְאַתֶּם‎ and shall ye be guiltless? 45:5; Ezek 20:31; 33:25b Jonah 4:11. So the וְ‎ consecutive and perfect (see 2a), Exod 5:5 וְהִשְׁבַּתֶּם‎ and will ye make them rest from their burdens? Num 16:10 וּבִקַּשְׁתֶּם‎ and seek ye the priesthood also? 1Sam 25:11; Isa 66:9; Psa 50:21 and shall I keep silence? Job 32:16 (compare Dr§ 119 γ).

g. attaching a fresh subj. (or object) to a clause already grammatically complete, it = and also, Gen 2:9b Num 16:2, 18 and they stood at the entrance of the tent of meeting, ואהרן ומשׁה‎ and Moses and Aaron (stood also), 16:27; Exod 35:22; Judg 6:5; Gen 1:16; b 12:17; 44:2; 46:15; Exod 29:3; Jer 32:29 (compare DrSm. i. 6, 11, & p. 293): when the idea thus attached is subordinate, or not logically embraced in the principal predicate, it approximates to the Arabic or 'waw of association' (followed by an accusative: WAG ii. § 37), Est 4:16 אָצוּם וְנַעֲרֹתַי אֲנִי‎ I will fast (singular) and (= with) my maidens, Exod 21:4; 1Sam 25:42; 29:10b (but insert here אַתָּה‎ with ᵐ5‎) 2Sam 12:30 (but read וּבָהּ‎, as 1Chr 20:2) 1Sam 20:10; Neh 6:12; Gen 4:20; Isa 42:5; Jer 19:1 (but read מזקני וְלָקַחְתָּ֫‎ with ᵐ5‎) 2Chr 2:3; 13:11; compare Jer 22:7 (וְכֵלָיו אִישׁ‎), Job 41:12. Whether Isa 48:16 וְרוּחוֺ‎ belongs here, is dubious

h. וְ‎ repeated = both . . . and (but גַּם ֗֗֗ גַּם‎) is more usual in this sense); Gen 34:28; Num 9:14; Josh 9:23; 2Sam 5:8 (text dubious), Isa 16:5; 38:15; Jer 13:14; 21:6; 32:14 (text dubious) 32:20; 40:8; Psa 76:7; Job 34:29; Dan 8:13; Neh 12:28.

i. a repetition of the same word with וְ‎ interposed expresses (a) diversity (rare), Deut 25:13 וָאֶבֶן אֶבֶן‎ a weight and a weight, i.e. different weights (explained by וּקְטַנָּה גְּדֹלָה‎), 25:14; Prov 20:23; Psa 12:3 וָלֵב בְּלֵב‎ with a heart and a heart = with a double heart, 1Chr 12:33 וָלֵב לֵב בְּלֹא‎; (b) distribution (except in וָדֹר דֹּר‎ Deut 32:7; Isa 13:20 +?Intr. 505) Psa 87:5; 1Chr 26:13 וָשָֽׁעַר׃ לְשַׁעַר‎ = for every gate, 28:14 (twice in verse); 2Chr 8:14; 34:13; 35:15; Ezra 10:14 וָעִיר עִיר זִקְנֵי‎ elders of every city, Neh 13:24; Est 1:8, 22 (twice in verse); 2:12; 3:4, 12 (4 t. in verse); 8:9 (twice in verse); strengthened by כָּלֿ‎2Chr 11:12 ועיר עיר בכל‎ in every several city, 19:5; 28:25; 31:19; 32:28; Est 2:11 ויום בכליֿום‎, 3:14; 4:3; 8:11, 13, 17 (twice in verse); 9:21, 27, 28; Psalm 45:18; Psa 145:13 (common in post-Biblical Hebrew, especially with כל‎).

j. it is used in the formulation of proverbs (the Vav adaequationis, הִשְׁתַּוָּאָה וָו‎) as Prov 17:3; 25:3, 20, 25 cold waters to a thirsty soul and good news from a far country (i.e. they are like each other), 26:3, 9, 14, 20; 27:21; Eccl 5:2; 7:1; 8:8; compare 9:11; Psa 19:5; 125:2; Job 14:11f.; 14:19 (compare in Arabic 'every man and his cares [accusative],' 'every thing and its price,' i.e. they go together: 'merchants and dogs [accusative] of Seleucia,' i.e. they are like one another: see FlKl. Schr. iii. 535 f.). More rarely in the opposite order, 5:7; 12:11. But 1Sam 12:15b cannot be thus explained: read with וּבְמַלְכְּכֶם ᵐ5‎, and see Dr.

k. in circumstantial clauses וְ‎ introduces a statement of the concomitant conditions under which the action denoted by the principal verb takes place: in such cases, the relation expressed by וְ‎ must often in English be stated explicitly by a conjunction, as when, since, seeing, though, etc., as occasion may require. So very often, as Gen 11:4 let us build a tower בַשָּׁמַיִם וְראֹשׁוֺ‎ and its top in the heavens (= with its top in etc.), 18:12 shall I have pleasure, זָקֵן וַאדֹנִי‎ and my lord is old (= my lord being old)? Judg 16:15 How sayest thou, I love thee, אִתִּי אֵין וְלִבְּךָ‎ and (= when) thy heart is not with me? and especially with a person pronoun, Gen 15:2 what wilt thou give me עֲרִירִי הֹלֵךְ וְאָנֹכִי‎ and I (= the case being that I) am going hence childless? 18:13; 20:3 lo, thou wilt die because of the woman thou hast taken בָּֽעַל׃ בְּעֻלַת וְהִוא‎ = seeing she is married, 24:62 ישֵׁב וְהוּא‎ = since or for he was dwelling (different from וַיֵּשֶׁב‎ = and he proceeded to dwell), 26:27 וְאַתֶּם‎ seeing ye hate me, Judg 13:9 and came to her ישֶׁבֶת וְהִיא‎ = as she was sitting, 1Sam 18:23; 1Kin 19:19 +? Psa 72:12 the afflicted לוֺ וְאֵיןעֹֿזֵר‎ and (= when) he has no helper (compare Job 29:12), Job 104:25 מִסְמָּר וְאֵין‎, Job 105:34; 5:9. See more fully Dr§ 156-60 Ges§ 141, R 2. (The analogous use of the is very common in Arabic: Wii. § 183.) Introducing an appeal to a fact confirmatory of some statement or promise, it almost = as truly as (compare Ew§ 340 c) Hosea 12:6 and J. is God of hosts, J. is his name! Joel 4:20; Amos 9:5-6 Isa 51:15 and I [who promise this] am J. thy God, who . . . . ! Jer 29:23; Psa 89:38b (compare in Qoran the frequently 'And God is .. . . . [the mighty, the merciful, etc.]').

2 The ו‎ consecutive (formerly called the Waw 'conversive'); —

a. with the

imperfect (וַּ‎ with following daghesh; before וָ א,‎), as וַיּאֹמֶר‎ properly = and he proceeded to say, chiefly in contin. of a preceding perfect tense (so Moabite);

b. with the

perfect (וְ‎, — in 1 & 2 singular, the tone, with certain exceptions [see Dr§ 110], being thrown forward to the ultima), as וְיָָֽשַׁבְתָּ֫‎ properly so [namely, as limited by a verb, or other term, preceding] hadst thou sat, chiefly in continuation of a preceding imperfect tense, in its various senses of future, jussive, or frequentative. Thefurther analysis of these idioms belongs to the grammar; see on a DrCh. vi., Ges§ 111, and on

b DrCh. viii. Ges§ 112. Here it must suffice to note — (a) ו‎ consecutive (especially with the imperfect) frequently couples two verbs in such a manner that the first, indicating the general character of the action, receives its closer definition in the second: in such cases, the first may often be represented in English by an adverb, as Gen 26:18 וַיַּחְמֹּר וַיָּשָׁב‎ and he turned and dug = and he dug again; so often; and similarly with הוֺסִיף‎ 25:1, מִהַר‎ 24:18, הוֺאִיל‎ Josh 7:7, etc.; more exceptionally, Gen 30:27; Est 8:6, and (not consecutive) Gen 47:6; Job 23:3; Song 2:3; Lam 3:26 (see Ges§ 120, 2 a; compare in Syriac Nö§ 335-6. In Arabic the stronger form of the conjugation here corresponds: Wii. § 140). (b) וַּ ‎ with the imperfect sometimes expresses a contrast = and yet, Gen 32:31 I have seen God face to face וַתִּנָּצֵל‎ and yet my soul is delivered, Deut 4:33; 2Sam 3:8; 19:29; Isa 51:12; Psa 73:14; 144:3; Job 10:8 + (compare Dr§ 74 β). (c) there is a tendency in the later books of the OT to use the perfect with simple וְ‎, where the classical language would employ the imperfect with וַּ ‎ (compare above

1); so especially in Ecclesiastes, where וַּ ‎ occurs thrice only, Job 1:17; 4:1, 7. (d) a double perfect with ו‎ consecutive is sometimes used, informally but neatly, with a hypothetical force; thus (a) in past or present time Exod 16:21 וְנָמָֽס׃ הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ וְחַם‎ and the sun used to be warm, and it used to melt = and if (or when) the sun was warm, it melted, 33:10; 1Kin 18:10; Jer 18:4, 8 וְנִחַמְתִּ֫י וְֹשָׁב‎ = and if it turns, I repent, 20:9 (see RV); (β) in future time, Gen 44:22 ומת אביו ועזב‎ and he will leave his father, and he will die = and if he leaves his father, he will die, 33:13; 42:38; Exod 4:14; 12:13; 1Sam 16:2; 19:3; Ezek 33:3; 39:15 etc. (Dr§ 147-9, Ges§ 159. 2 e).

3 With a

voluntative (cohortative or jussive) וְ‎ expresses an intention, that or so that (an elegancy by which the too frequent use of לְמַעַן‎ or בַּעֲבוּר‎ is avoided): Exod 10:17 entreat God, וְיָסֵר‎ so may he remove (= that he may remove) this death, Gen 27:4 and bring it me וְאֹכֵ֑לָה‎ so let me eat (= that I may eat); and without the modal form being externally indicated, Exod 14:1 speak . . . וְיָשֻׁבוּ‎ that they return, 14:15; and often Sts. even of past time, as 1Kin 13:33 whom he would, he consecrated וִיהִי‎ that there might be priests of the high places, 2Kin 19:25; Isa 25:9 a Lam 1:19. After a negative, Psa 51:18 thou desirest not sacrifice, וְאֶתֵּ֑נָה‎ so [= in that case] would I give it (or, that I might give it), 55:13 וְאֶשָּׂא‎ so could I bear it (or, that I might bear it), Isa 53:2 RVm Num 23:19; Jer 5:28 RV. Sts. also before an imperative, Gen 12:2 and be (= that thou mayest be) a blessing, 2Sam 21:3 +. See more fully Dr§ 59-65, Ges§ 108. 2; 109. 2; 110. 2. (In Arabic with the subjunctive is used similarly: Wii. § 15 d.) A volunt. is also sometimes attached by וְ‎ to a preceding volunt. or imperative, so as to form a virtually hypothetical sentence, as Gen 42:18 וִחְיוּ עֲשׂוּ זֹאת‎ = if you do this, you shall live, 30:28; 34:12; Prov 3:9f. 4:4, 8; Isa 55:2: see Dr§ 152.

4 It expresses often an informal inference, or consequence, so, then, especially at the beginning of a speech: Gen 27:8; Psa 2:10 and often וְעַתָּה‎ now, therefore; וְלָמָּה‎ and וּמַדּוּעַ‎ why, then? Gen 29:25; Num 12:8; 16:3 +; Exod 2:20 וְאַיּוֺ‎ where, then, is he? Gen 34:21; 1Sam 15:14; 26:22 וְיַעֲבֹר‎ let, then, . . . come over, 2Sam 24:3; 2Kin 4:41 קֶמַח וּקְחוּ‎ then bring meal, Ezek 18:32. So the וְ‎ consecutive and the perfect, as Deut 2:4 וְנִשְׁמַרְתֶּם‎ take heed, therefore, 4:15; 7:9 וְיָָֽדַעְתָּ֫‎ know, therefore, 30:19; 1Sam 6:5; 1Kin 2:6; Ruth 3:9; Josh 15:19; Isa 40:6b (Dr§ 119 δ).

5 ו‎ introduces the predicate or apodosis: namely

a. וְ‎ consecutive and the Perfect — in answer to אִם‎ or כִּי‎ constantly, as Exod 19:5; 23:22 if thou hearkenest to my voice, וְאָֽיַבְתִּ֫י‎ then am I (= I will be) enemy to thy enemies (see Dr§ 136-8); after the casus pendens, 12:44 every servant that is bought for money, וּמַלְתָּ֫ה‎ thou shalt circumcise him, etc. Num 14:31; 24:24; 1Sam 25:27; 2Sam 14:10 he that spake unto thee, אֵלַי וַהֲבֵאתוֺ‎ so hast thou brought him (= thou shalt bring him) unto me, Isa 9:4; 56:6f. +; Exod 12:15; 31:14; Deut 17:12 +; after various time-determinations, as Gen 3:5 in the day of your eating from it וְנִפְקְחוּ‎ then shall your eyes be opened, Exod 16:6 וִידַעְתֶּם עֶרֶב‎ at even, then shall ye know, 16:7; 32:34; 2Sam 15:10; 1Kin 13:31 אֹתִי וּקְבַרְתֶּם בְּמוֺתִי‎ when I die, so ye shall bury me, etc., + often; after conjs., as כִּי‎ Gen 29:15, יַעַן‎ 1Kin 20:28; Isa 3:16f., תַּחַת‎ 60:15, etc., (see Dr§ 123).

b. וַּ ‎ consecutive and the imperfect (but much less frequently than the perfect), as Gen 30:30 the little that thou hadst, וַיִּפְרֹץ‎ it hath increased, Exod 9:21; 2Sam 4:10; 1Kin 9:20f. 15:13 +; after time-determinations, Gen 22:4 on the third day וַיִּשָּׂא‎ then Abraham lifted up his eyes, 19:15; 27:34; 37:18; 1Sam 6:6; 12:8; Isa 6:1; Hosea 11:1 when Israel was a child, וָאֹהֲבֵהוּ‎ then I loved him, +; occasionally after conjunctions, as כַּאֲשֶׁר‎ Exod 16:34, יַעַן‎ 1Sam 15:23, לְמַעַן‎ Isa 45:4, אִם‎ Psa 59:16 (Dr§ 127).

c. in other cases (not 'consecutive') — all more or less uncommon: namely a. וְ‎ closely joined to the imperfect Gen 13:9 if to the left, וְאֵימִינָה‎ then I will take the right (compare 2Sam 12:8) Exod 12:3 on the 10th of the month וְיִקְחוּ‎ then let them take, Num 16:5; Isa 43:4; Hosea 4:6; 10:10; Psa 69:33; Job 15:17; 2Sam 22:41; Prov 23:24 Kt (Dr§ 125); β. separated from the verb, Exod 8:22; Lev 7:16 יֵאָכֵל וְהַנּוֺתָר וּמִמָּחֳרָת‎ and on the morrow, then the remainder shall be eaten, Josh 3:3; 1Kin 8:32; Isa 8:7; 48:7; Job 14:7; 20:18; b 23:12; 25:5; 32:14 +; γ. without a verb, Gen 40:9 וְהִנֵּה בַּחֲלֹמִי‎ in my dream, behold, a vine was before me, 40:16; 2Sam 23:3f.; Prov 10:25, and the extreme cases 2Sam 15:34 thy father's slave, מֵאָז וַאֲנִי‎ I was that of old, — but now עַבְדְּךָ וַאֲנִי‎ well, I will be thine, Isa 34:12 (si vera lectio), Job 4:6b דְּרָכֶיךָ וְתֹם תִּקְוָָֽתְךָ‎ thy confidence — it is the uprightness of thy ways, 36:26 חֵקֶר וְלֹא שָׁנָיו מִסְמַּר‎ Ges. seine Jahre, da ist kein Zählen (compare Dr§ 124-5, 128-9). — With 4, 5 compare the Arabic , Wi. § 366 b, 367 c; ii. § 187; Dr§ 185 end.

צקלג.def:
H6860. Tsiqelag

ִצקְלַג‎ and (1Chr 12:1; 12:21 ׳צִיק‎)

proper name, of a location (צִ֒קלָ֑ג‎ 1Sam 27:6 a +, ִצקְלָג֖‎ 2Sam 2:1 צִיקְלָ֔ג‎ 1Chr 12:1); — assigned to Judah Josh 15:31, to Simeon 19:5; Philistine city given to David 1Sam 27:6 (twice in verse); 30:1 (3 t. in verse); 30:14, 26; 2Sam 1:1; 4:10; 1Chr 4:30; 12:1; 12:21 (van d. H. v.12:20); Σεκελακ, Σικελαγ, etc.; usually identified with Zuheilikah, 19 miles southwest from Bêt Jibrin, 11 miles east-southeast from Gaza (compare BuhlGeogr. 185).

צקלון.def:
H6861. tsiqqalon

[צִקָּלֹן‎] noun [masculine] doubtful word; — suffix כַרְמֶל בְּצִקְנֹוֺ‎ 2Kin 4:42 ᵑ7 ᵑ6‎ garment; ᵐ5‎ omitted, but A βακελλεθ, Arm. bakela θ whence LagArmen. Stud. § 333, M. i. 212 reads (plausibly) בִּקְלַעְתּוֺ‎ in his wallet, Arabic , , and so ᵑ9‎ pera.

צרה.def:
H6869. tsarah

I. צָרָה‎72 noun feminine id.; — absolute ׳צ‎ 1Sam 26:24 +, צָרָתָה‎ Psa 120:1 (Ges§ 90g); construct צָרַת‎ Gen 42:21; suffix צָרָתִי‎ 35:3 +, צָרַתְכֶם‎ Judg 10:14, etc.; plural צָרוֺת‎ absolute Isa 65:16 +; suffix צָרֹתֵיכֶם‎ 1Sam 10:19, etc.; — straits, distress, Gen 42:21 (E), 1Sam 26:24; 2Sam 4:9; 1Kin 1:29; Isa 8:22; Job 5:19; 27:9; especially Psalms (24 t.), e.g. 22:12; Job 25:17 (see רחב‎), Job 25:22; 31:8; 34:17-18, specifically of travail, וַחֲבָלִים צָרָה‎ Jer 49:24 (simile), compare 4:31 (Gie צְוָחָה‎, after ᵐ5‎); נַפְשׁוֺ צָרַת‎ Gen 42:21 (E); צָרָתִי בְּיוֺם‎ 35:3 (E), Psa 77:3; 86:7, compare 2Kin 19:3 = Isa 37:3; Psa 20:2; 50:15; Prov 24:10; 25:19; Jer 16:19; Obadiah 12, 14; Nahum 1:7; Hab 3:16, צ ׳יוֺם וּמְצוּקָה‎ Zeph 1:15; בְּעֵתצָֿרַתְכֶם‎ Judg 10:14, compare Neh 9:27; Psa 37:39; Isa 33:2; Jer 14:8; 15:11; 30:7; Dan 12:1; also בַּצָּרָה‎ Psa 81:8, בְּצָרָה‎ 91:15; Neh 9:37, בְּצָדוֺת‎ Psa 46:2, etc.; וְצָרוֺת רָעוֺת‎ Deut 31:17, 21 compare 1Sam 10:19; Psa 71:20, וְצוּקָה צָרָה‎ Prov 1:27, צ ׳אֶרֶץ ׳וְצ‎ Isa 30:6; with ל‎ (poetry), לִי בַּצָּרָ֫תָה‎ Psa 120:1 in my distress, לִי מִצָּרָה‎ Jonah 2:3. — צָרָה‎ Zech 10:11, read מִצְרַיִם‎ [or מָצוֺר‎] We Now GASm; צֹ֫רָה‎ KloThLz, 1879, 566 StaZAW i (1881), 22; Psa 9:10; 10:1 see בַּצָּרָה‎.

II. [צָרָה‎] noun feminine vexer, rival-wife (see references below √; also Ecclus 37:11); — suffix צָרָתָהּ‎ 1Sam 1:6.

צרויה.def:
H6870. Tseruyah

צְרוּיָה‎ proper name, feminine Σαρουια: mother of Abishai, Joab and Asahel; — ׳צ‎ 1Sam 26:6 +, צְרֻיָה‎ 2Sam 14:1; 16:10; 23:37; — according to 1Chr 2:16 a she was David's sister; called יוֺאָב אֵם‎ 2Sam 17:25; elsewhere after construct בֶּןֿ‎ (בְּנֵי‎): ׳בֶּןצֿ‎ of Abishai 1Sam 26:6; 2Sam 16:9; 18:2; 19:22; 21:17; 1Chr 18:12; of Joab 2Sam 2:13; 8:16 = 1Chr 18:15; 2Sam 14:1; 23:18 and 23:37 = 1Chr 11:39; 1Kin 1:7; 2:5, 22; 1Chr 11:6; 26:28; 27:24; plural of all three 2Sam 2:18; 1Chr 2:16; Abishai and Joab 2Sam 3:39; 16:10; 19:23.

צרור.def:
H6872. tsrowr

I. צְרוֺר‎ noun masculineHag 1:6 bundle, parcel, pouch, bag (properly a binding, i.e. something bound up); — ׳צ‎ absolute Amos 9:9 +, construct Gen 42:35 +; plural construct צְרֹרוֺת‎ 42:35; — bundle or pouch (purse) of money 42:35 (twice in verse) (E), Prov 7:20; ׳צ הַמֹּר‎ Song 1:13 (figurative of lover); הַחַיִּים בִּצ ׳צְרוּרָה‎ 1Sam 25:29 (figurative; see I. צרר‎); בִּצ ׳חָתֻם מִּשְׁעִי‎ Job 14:17 (i.e. hidden, forgotten Hi Bu and others; > al. treasured up), ׳צ נָקוּב‎ Hag 1:6 (see I. נקב‎).

II. צְרוֺר‎ noun masculine pebble; — ׳צ‎ 2Sam 17:13; also Amos 9:9 (where perhaps figurative for grain of wheat, in metaphor of winnowed Israel, compare Dr Now and others; > pebble retained in sieve PreuschemZAW xv (1895), 24, compare on custom WetzstZPV xiv (1891), f.).

III. צְרוֺר‎ proper name, masculine grandfather of Kish 1Sam 9:1, Αρεδ, ᵐ5‎ of L Σαρα.

H6873. tsarach

Qal Participle active גִּבּוֺר שָׁם צֹרֵחַ מַר‎ Zeph 1:14 bitterly roareth there a hero, but abrupt in context and improbable; Gr (in part after ᵐ5‎) conjectures י ׳קוֺל כַּגִּבּוֺר יִצְרַח‎ (compare Hiph`il).

Hiph`il Imperfect3masculine singular יַצְרִיחַ‎ Isa 42:13 utter a roar (of ׳י‎, going to battle; || יָרִיעַ‎).

צריח.def:
H6877. tseriach

צְרִיחַ‎ noun [masculine] perhaps excavation, underground chamber; — ׳צ‎ absolute Judg 9:49, construct 9:46; plural צְרִחִים‎ 1Sam 13:6; — used as hiding-places 13:6 (+ בֹּרוֺת סְלָעִים, חֲוָחִים, מְעָרוֺת,‎); as refuge Judg 9:46 (where connected with shrine), 9:49 (Vrss stronghold; on uncertainty of meaning see GFM).

צֹרִי‎ see I. צֹר‎. צְרֻיָה צְרִי, צֳרִי,‎ see צרה‎. above,

צרך‎ (√ of following; Late Hebrew צָרַךְ‎ have need of; Arabic be needy, so Aramaic צְרַךְ‎, (צ‎, = !); Christian-Palestinian Aramaic χρεία).

צרך.def:
ו‎

ו‎, Waw, sixth letter; in modern Hebrew = numeral 6; no evidence of this usage in OT times.

וָ וּ, וְ,‎

demonstrative adverb and

conjunction so, then, and (Phoenician, Moabite, Aramaic ו‎; Arabic ; Ethiopic Assyrian u DlW (but between verbs the usually connective is the enclitic ma KAT2. 508, Dl§§ 82, 150). The use in Hebrew shews that original וְ‎ was not a merely copulative conjunction, but that it possessed a demonstrative force (compare Dr§ 122), which is often perceptible as such, though in other cases, from its being applied to denote mere juxtaposition or connection [compare Greek τε, and Latin tum .... tum = 'both .... and,' both properly demonstratives: Assyrian ma has also a demonstrative force, Dl§ 79], it is less palpable) — וְ‎ before shwa' mobile or a labial is vocalized וּ‎; often before a tone-syll., when the word itself has a disj. accent, וָ‎ (as וַָמתִּי׃‎ Gen 19:19; וָמֵ֖תוּ‎ 33:13; וָמֵ֑ת‎ 44:9; וָחָֽיָה׃‎ Exod 1:16; וָיָ֑מָּה‎ Josh 15:46; וָ֔לֹ֕א‎ 2Sam 13:26; וָאָ֖רֶץ‎ Isa 26:19; וָקָ֔מוּ‎ 49:7; וָחָֽתָּה׃‎ Jer 48:1; וָרָֹע‎ Psa 10:15); especially when it forms with the preceding word a pair, whether of parallel or opposed ideas (as וָכֹה כֹּה‎ Exod 2:12, וָמִ֖י מִי‎ 10:8, וָאָ֑בֶן אֶבֶן‎ Deut 25:13; וָדֹ֑ר דֹּר‎ 32:7 +; וָבֹ֔הוּ תֹּהוּ‎ Gen 1:2, וָרֶמֶ֛שׂ בְּהֵמָה‎ 1:24, וָרָֽע׃ טוֺב‎ 2:19, וָנָ֖ד נָע‎ 4:12, וָלָ֖יְלָה וְיוֺם וָחֹ֛רֶף וְקַיִץ‎ 8:22, וֵָלךְ׃ קַח‎ 12:19, וָאָֽרֶץ׃ שָׁמַיִם‎ 14:19, וָאָ֑תָּה אֲנִי‎ 31:44, וָה֑וּא אֲנִי‎ 41:11, וָשׁוּבוּ עִבְרוּ‎ Exod 32:27, וָהֵ֛ם אַתָּה‎ Num 16:16, וָמֶ֑לָךְ אֱלֹהִים‎ 1Kin 21:13, וָנֶ֖כֶד נִין‎ Isa 14:22, וָשֶׁ֖בֶר שֹׁד‎ 59:7; and often: see more fully Bö§ 600); occasionally also with a conjunctive accent (as לְעֹלָֽם׃ וָשַחי‎ Gen 3:22 compare Lev 18:5, שָׁם וָמַ֣תְנוּ‎ 2Kin 7:4, חֲדָשָׁ֑ה וָאָ֣רֶץ‎ Isa 65:17; Prov 25:3, גָּדוֺל׃ וָשֶשׁבֶר שֹׁ֖ד‎ Jer 48:3, compare 32:29). — וְ‎ is used very freely and widely in Hebrew, but also with much delicacy, to express relations and shades of meaning which Western languages would usually indicate by distinct particles. But in Hebrew particles such as לָכֵן לְמַעַן, בַּעֲבוּר, אוּלָם, אָכֵן, אַךְ, אָז, אוֺ,‎, etc., were reserved for cases in which special emphasis or distinctness was desired: their frequent use was felt instinctively to be inconsistent with the lightness and grace of movement which the Hebrew ear loved; and thus in AV, RV, words like or, then, but, notwithstanding, howbeit, so, thus, therefore, that, constantly appear, where the Hebrew has simply וְ‎.

1 And, connecting both words (see above), and sentences (Gen 1:5 וג קָרָא ׳וְלַחשֶׁךְ‎). When three, four, or more words follow, the conjunction may connect them all, as 7:21; 10:2 (6 t.) 24:35 (7 t.) Josh 7:24 (10 t.) 2Sam 17:28f.: often however it is prefixed only to the last, as Gen 5:32; 10:1; Deut 18:10 etc.; occas. even it connects only the first two, 1Kin 8:47; Isa 1:13; Psa 45:9; Job 42:9. Remarkably, however, וְ‎ as a mere conjunction is, as a rule, not in classical Hebrew attached directly to verbs (especially in the perfect), the construction with וְ‎ consecutive (see

2) being (as in Moabite) preferred: thus וַיִּבֶן יָצָא‎ is said, not וּבָנָה יָצָא‎. Exceptions in classical Hebrew are (a) sometimes where synonyms are coupled, as Num 23:19 וְדִבֶּר ֗֗֗ אָמַר‎, Deut 2:30; Judg 5:26; 1Sam 12:2; Isa 1:2 ורוממתי גדּלתי‎ 2:11; 5:14; 8:8; 19:6; 29:20; (b) isolated cases, difficult to reduce to rule (perhaps sometimes due to textual error), as Gen 28:6; 38:5; Judg 3:23; 7:13; 16:18; 1Sam 1:12; 3:13; 4:19; 5:7; 10:9; 17:38, 48; 25:20 and elsewhere (in other passages, apparently similar, the perfect and וְ‎ has a frequent. force (see 2), as Gen 37:3; Exod 36:29f.; Num 10:17f. 21:15, 20; 1Sam 2:22; 16:14; 17:34f. (see Dr) 27:9; 2Sam 16:13; 17:17, perhaps also Gen 15:6; 21:25; 34:5). In later parts of OT, probably through Aramaic influence, the perfect with simple וְ‎ occurs more frequently: so especially in Ecclesiastes, where it is all but universal (e.g. 2:11-12, 13, 15 etc.). With the imperfect, the simple וְ‎ is not so unidiomatic, even in classical Hebrew (compare 3); see 1:9, 26; 9:27; 17:2; 22:17; 27:29; Exod 23:8 (frequently) 24:7; Num 14:12; Deut 17:13; 30:12-13, Josh 3:13; 7:3; Judg 7:3; 13:8; Isa 5:29; 14:10; often also in Jeremiah, Isa2, Job, Psalms, e.g. 40:30; 41:20 (Dr§ 116: contrast 28:13). See more fully Dr§ 130-4 Ges§ 112. 6. Special senses: —

a. it sometimes = and specially, Gen 3:16; 1Kin 11:1 many strange women, and specially the daughter of Pharaoh, Isa 1:1 Judah and (= and particularly) Jerusalem, 2:1; 9:7; Psa 18:1.

b. and in particular ('und zwar'), and that (explicative), Gen 4:4; Judg 7:22; 1Sam 17:40 וּבַיַּלְקוּט‎, 28:3 in Ramah, and that in his city (unusual: text suspicious), 2Sam 13:20 וְשֹׁמֵמָה‎ and that desolate, Isa 57:11 I have been silent וּמֵעוֺלָם‎ and that from of old, 32:7; Jer 15:13; Amos 3:11 (si vera lectio), 4:10; Zech 9:9b Mal 1:11; Psa 68:10; Prov 3:12; Lam 3:26; Eccl 8:2; Dan 1:3; 8:10; 9:25, 27; Neh 8:13; 1Chr 9:27; 2Chr 8:13; 29:27 (but' even' for ו‎, before ל‎ and infinitive, e.g. in Isa 44:28; Jer 17:10; 19:12, is wrong; see Ew§ 351 c, Dr§ 206).

c. sometimes it introduces an idea which so exceeds or adds to what has preceded, that it is nearly equivalent to also, 1Sam 25:43; 1Kin 2:22 ask also the kingdom for him; unusually Hosea 8:6 והוא מישׂראל כי‎ for of Israel is it also, Eccl 5:6 והבלים‎ (see De) 2Chr 27:5 (but see ᵐ5‎). Or it may be rendered yea: so especially in the ascending numerations 3-4 Amos 1:3, 6, 9, 11, 13; 2:1, 4, 6; Prov 30:18, 21, 29, 6-7 6:16; Job 5:19, 7-8 Micah 5:4 — the first number being aggravated, or augmented, by a higher. In one idiom וּגְבוּל‎, occurring in geographic descriptions, it is used peculiarly, seemingly = at the same time: Num 34:6 and as for the western border, וּגְבוּל הַגָּדוֺל הַיָּם לָכֶם וְהָיָה‎ the great sea shall be to you also (German 'zugleich') a border, Deut 3:16 וּגְבוּל הַנַּחַל תּוֺךְ‎ the middle of the stream being at the same time the border, 3:17; Josh 13:23, 27; 15:12, 47 (but these, except Num 34:6, might be cases of 5c γ).

d. it connects alternative cases, so that it = or: Exod 20:10, 17; 21:16 he that stealeth a man בְיָדוֺ וְנִמְצָא וּמְכָרוֺ‎ and selleth him, and (= or if) he be found in his hand, 21:17; Lev 21:14; 22:23-24, Prov 29:9 (Fl Ew RV: whether . . . or) Job 31:13, 16, 26, etc.

e. it connects contrasted ideas, where in our idiom the contrast would be expressed explicitly by but; in such cases prominence is usually given to the contrasted idea by its being placed immediately after the conjunction: Gen 2:17 but of the tree of the knowledge . . . thou shalt not eat, 4:2, 5; 6:8; 17:21; 31:10 etc., 1Kin 2:26; 10:7; 11:32, 34; 15:14; Prov 10:1-2, 3, 4 + often; even after לֹא‎ (where כִּי‎ or אִם כִּי‎ might be expected), as Gen 42:10; Exod 21:18; Lev 26:45; Deut 11:11; Judg 19:12; 1Kin 3:11.

f. it introduces a contrasted idea in such a way as to suggest a question, especially before a pronoun, Judg 14:16 I told it not to my father or my mother, אַגִּיד וְלָךְ‎ and shall I told it unto thee? 2Sam 11:11; Jer 25:29 תִנָּקוּ הִנָּקֵה וְאַתֶּם‎ and shall ye be guiltless? 45:5; Ezek 20:31; 33:25b Jonah 4:11. So the וְ‎ consecutive and perfect (see 2a), Exod 5:5 וְהִשְׁבַּתֶּם‎ and will ye make them rest from their burdens? Num 16:10 וּבִקַּשְׁתֶּם‎ and seek ye the priesthood also? 1Sam 25:11; Isa 66:9; Psa 50:21 and shall I keep silence? Job 32:16 (compare Dr§ 119 γ).

g. attaching a fresh subj. (or object) to a clause already grammatically complete, it = and also, Gen 2:9b Num 16:2, 18 and they stood at the entrance of the tent of meeting, ואהרן ומשׁה‎ and Moses and Aaron (stood also), 16:27; Exod 35:22; Judg 6:5; Gen 1:16; b 12:17; 44:2; 46:15; Exod 29:3; Jer 32:29 (compare DrSm. i. 6, 11, & p. 293): when the idea thus attached is subordinate, or not logically embraced in the principal predicate, it approximates to the Arabic or 'waw of association' (followed by an accusative: WAG ii. § 37), Est 4:16 אָצוּם וְנַעֲרֹתַי אֲנִי‎ I will fast (singular) and (= with) my maidens, Exod 21:4; 1Sam 25:42; 29:10b (but insert here אַתָּה‎ with ᵐ5‎) 2Sam 12:30 (but read וּבָהּ‎, as 1Chr 20:2) 1Sam 20:10; Neh 6:12; Gen 4:20; Isa 42:5; Jer 19:1 (but read מזקני וְלָקַחְתָּ֫‎ with ᵐ5‎) 2Chr 2:3; 13:11; compare Jer 22:7 (וְכֵלָיו אִישׁ‎), Job 41:12. Whether Isa 48:16 וְרוּחוֺ‎ belongs here, is dubious

h. וְ‎ repeated = both . . . and (but גַּם ֗֗֗ גַּם‎) is more usual in this sense); Gen 34:28; Num 9:14; Josh 9:23; 2Sam 5:8 (text dubious), Isa 16:5; 38:15; Jer 13:14; 21:6; 32:14 (text dubious) 32:20; 40:8; Psa 76:7; Job 34:29; Dan 8:13; Neh 12:28.

i. a repetition of the same word with וְ‎ interposed expresses (a) diversity (rare), Deut 25:13 וָאֶבֶן אֶבֶן‎ a weight and a weight, i.e. different weights (explained by וּקְטַנָּה גְּדֹלָה‎), 25:14; Prov 20:23; Psa 12:3 וָלֵב בְּלֵב‎ with a heart and a heart = with a double heart, 1Chr 12:33 וָלֵב לֵב בְּלֹא‎; (b) distribution (except in וָדֹר דֹּר‎ Deut 32:7; Isa 13:20 +?Intr. 505) Psa 87:5; 1Chr 26:13 וָשָֽׁעַר׃ לְשַׁעַר‎ = for every gate, 28:14 (twice in verse); 2Chr 8:14; 34:13; 35:15; Ezra 10:14 וָעִיר עִיר זִקְנֵי‎ elders of every city, Neh 13:24; Est 1:8, 22 (twice in verse); 2:12; 3:4, 12 (4 t. in verse); 8:9 (twice in verse); strengthened by כָּלֿ‎2Chr 11:12 ועיר עיר בכל‎ in every several city, 19:5; 28:25; 31:19; 32:28; Est 2:11 ויום בכליֿום‎, 3:14; 4:3; 8:11, 13, 17 (twice in verse); 9:21, 27, 28; Psalm 45:18; Psa 145:13 (common in post-Biblical Hebrew, especially with כל‎).

j. it is used in the formulation of proverbs (the Vav adaequationis, הִשְׁתַּוָּאָה וָו‎) as Prov 17:3; 25:3, 20, 25 cold waters to a thirsty soul and good news from a far country (i.e. they are like each other), 26:3, 9, 14, 20; 27:21; Eccl 5:2; 7:1; 8:8; compare 9:11; Psa 19:5; 125:2; Job 14:11f.; 14:19 (compare in Arabic 'every man and his cares [accusative],' 'every thing and its price,' i.e. they go together: 'merchants and dogs [accusative] of Seleucia,' i.e. they are like one another: see FlKl. Schr. iii. 535 f.). More rarely in the opposite order, 5:7; 12:11. But 1Sam 12:15b cannot be thus explained: read with וּבְמַלְכְּכֶם ᵐ5‎, and see Dr.

k. in circumstantial clauses וְ‎ introduces a statement of the concomitant conditions under which the action denoted by the principal verb takes place: in such cases, the relation expressed by וְ‎ must often in English be stated explicitly by a conjunction, as when, since, seeing, though, etc., as occasion may require. So very often, as Gen 11:4 let us build a tower בַשָּׁמַיִם וְראֹשׁוֺ‎ and its top in the heavens (= with its top in etc.), 18:12 shall I have pleasure, זָקֵן וַאדֹנִי‎ and my lord is old (= my lord being old)? Judg 16:15 How sayest thou, I love thee, אִתִּי אֵין וְלִבְּךָ‎ and (= when) thy heart is not with me? and especially with a person pronoun, Gen 15:2 what wilt thou give me עֲרִירִי הֹלֵךְ וְאָנֹכִי‎ and I (= the case being that I) am going hence childless? 18:13; 20:3 lo, thou wilt die because of the woman thou hast taken בָּֽעַל׃ בְּעֻלַת וְהִוא‎ = seeing she is married, 24:62 ישֵׁב וְהוּא‎ = since or for he was dwelling (different from וַיֵּשֶׁב‎ = and he proceeded to dwell), 26:27 וְאַתֶּם‎ seeing ye hate me, Judg 13:9 and came to her ישֶׁבֶת וְהִיא‎ = as she was sitting, 1Sam 18:23; 1Kin 19:19 +? Psa 72:12 the afflicted לוֺ וְאֵיןעֹֿזֵר‎ and (= when) he has no helper (compare Job 29:12), Job 104:25 מִסְמָּר וְאֵין‎, Job 105:34; 5:9. See more fully Dr§ 156-60 Ges§ 141, R 2. (The analogous use of the is very common in Arabic: Wii. § 183.) Introducing an appeal to a fact confirmatory of some statement or promise, it almost = as truly as (compare Ew§ 340 c) Hosea 12:6 and J. is God of hosts, J. is his name! Joel 4:20; Amos 9:5-6 Isa 51:15 and I [who promise this] am J. thy God, who . . . . ! Jer 29:23; Psa 89:38b (compare in Qoran the frequently 'And God is .. . . . [the mighty, the merciful, etc.]').

2 The ו‎ consecutive (formerly called the Waw 'conversive'); —

a. with the

imperfect (וַּ‎ with following daghesh; before וָ א,‎), as וַיּאֹמֶר‎ properly = and he proceeded to say, chiefly in contin. of a preceding perfect tense (so Moabite);

b. with the

perfect (וְ‎, — in 1 & 2 singular, the tone, with certain exceptions [see Dr§ 110], being thrown forward to the ultima), as וְיָָֽשַׁבְתָּ֫‎ properly so [namely, as limited by a verb, or other term, preceding] hadst thou sat, chiefly in continuation of a preceding imperfect tense, in its various senses of future, jussive, or frequentative. Thefurther analysis of these idioms belongs to the grammar; see on a DrCh. vi., Ges§ 111, and on

b DrCh. viii. Ges§ 112. Here it must suffice to note — (a) ו‎ consecutive (especially with the imperfect) frequently couples two verbs in such a manner that the first, indicating the general character of the action, receives its closer definition in the second: in such cases, the first may often be represented in English by an adverb, as Gen 26:18 וַיַּחְמֹּר וַיָּשָׁב‎ and he turned and dug = and he dug again; so often; and similarly with הוֺסִיף‎ 25:1, מִהַר‎ 24:18, הוֺאִיל‎ Josh 7:7, etc.; more exceptionally, Gen 30:27; Est 8:6, and (not consecutive) Gen 47:6; Job 23:3; Song 2:3; Lam 3:26 (see Ges§ 120, 2 a; compare in Syriac Nö§ 335-6. In Arabic the stronger form of the conjugation here corresponds: Wii. § 140). (b) וַּ ‎ with the imperfect sometimes expresses a contrast = and yet, Gen 32:31 I have seen God face to face וַתִּנָּצֵל‎ and yet my soul is delivered, Deut 4:33; 2Sam 3:8; 19:29; Isa 51:12; Psa 73:14; 144:3; Job 10:8 + (compare Dr§ 74 β). (c) there is a tendency in the later books of the OT to use the perfect with simple וְ‎, where the classical language would employ the imperfect with וַּ ‎ (compare above

1); so especially in Ecclesiastes, where וַּ ‎ occurs thrice only, Job 1:17; 4:1, 7. (d) a double perfect with ו‎ consecutive is sometimes used, informally but neatly, with a hypothetical force; thus (a) in past or present time Exod 16:21 וְנָמָֽס׃ הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ וְחַם‎ and the sun used to be warm, and it used to melt = and if (or when) the sun was warm, it melted, 33:10; 1Kin 18:10; Jer 18:4, 8 וְנִחַמְתִּ֫י וְֹשָׁב‎ = and if it turns, I repent, 20:9 (see RV); (β) in future time, Gen 44:22 ומת אביו ועזב‎ and he will leave his father, and he will die = and if he leaves his father, he will die, 33:13; 42:38; Exod 4:14; 12:13; 1Sam 16:2; 19:3; Ezek 33:3; 39:15 etc. (Dr§ 147-9, Ges§ 159. 2 e).

3 With a

voluntative (cohortative or jussive) וְ‎ expresses an intention, that or so that (an elegancy by which the too frequent use of לְמַעַן‎ or בַּעֲבוּר‎ is avoided): Exod 10:17 entreat God, וְיָסֵר‎ so may he remove (= that he may remove) this death, Gen 27:4 and bring it me וְאֹכֵ֑לָה‎ so let me eat (= that I may eat); and without the modal form being externally indicated, Exod 14:1 speak . . . וְיָשֻׁבוּ‎ that they return, 14:15; and often Sts. even of past time, as 1Kin 13:33 whom he would, he consecrated וִיהִי‎ that there might be priests of the high places, 2Kin 19:25; Isa 25:9 a Lam 1:19. After a negative, Psa 51:18 thou desirest not sacrifice, וְאֶתֵּ֑נָה‎ so [= in that case] would I give it (or, that I might give it), 55:13 וְאֶשָּׂא‎ so could I bear it (or, that I might bear it), Isa 53:2 RVm Num 23:19; Jer 5:28 RV. Sts. also before an imperative, Gen 12:2 and be (= that thou mayest be) a blessing, 2Sam 21:3 +. See more fully Dr§ 59-65, Ges§ 108. 2; 109. 2; 110. 2. (In Arabic with the subjunctive is used similarly: Wii. § 15 d.) A volunt. is also sometimes attached by וְ‎ to a preceding volunt. or imperative, so as to form a virtually hypothetical sentence, as Gen 42:18 וִחְיוּ עֲשׂוּ זֹאת‎ = if you do this, you shall live, 30:28; 34:12; Prov 3:9f. 4:4, 8; Isa 55:2: see Dr§ 152.

4 It expresses often an informal inference, or consequence, so, then, especially at the beginning of a speech: Gen 27:8; Psa 2:10 and often וְעַתָּה‎ now, therefore; וְלָמָּה‎ and וּמַדּוּעַ‎ why, then? Gen 29:25; Num 12:8; 16:3 +; Exod 2:20 וְאַיּוֺ‎ where, then, is he? Gen 34:21; 1Sam 15:14; 26:22 וְיַעֲבֹר‎ let, then, . . . come over, 2Sam 24:3; 2Kin 4:41 קֶמַח וּקְחוּ‎ then bring meal, Ezek 18:32. So the וְ‎ consecutive and the perfect, as Deut 2:4 וְנִשְׁמַרְתֶּם‎ take heed, therefore, 4:15; 7:9 וְיָָֽדַעְתָּ֫‎ know, therefore, 30:19; 1Sam 6:5; 1Kin 2:6; Ruth 3:9; Josh 15:19; Isa 40:6b (Dr§ 119 δ).

5 ו‎ introduces the predicate or apodosis: namely

a. וְ‎ consecutive and the Perfect — in answer to אִם‎ or כִּי‎ constantly, as Exod 19:5; 23:22 if thou hearkenest to my voice, וְאָֽיַבְתִּ֫י‎ then am I (= I will be) enemy to thy enemies (see Dr§ 136-8); after the casus pendens, 12:44 every servant that is bought for money, וּמַלְתָּ֫ה‎ thou shalt circumcise him, etc. Num 14:31; 24:24; 1Sam 25:27; 2Sam 14:10 he that spake unto thee, אֵלַי וַהֲבֵאתוֺ‎ so hast thou brought him (= thou shalt bring him) unto me, Isa 9:4; 56:6f. +; Exod 12:15; 31:14; Deut 17:12 +; after various time-determinations, as Gen 3:5 in the day of your eating from it וְנִפְקְחוּ‎ then shall your eyes be opened, Exod 16:6 וִידַעְתֶּם עֶרֶב‎ at even, then shall ye know, 16:7; 32:34; 2Sam 15:10; 1Kin 13:31 אֹתִי וּקְבַרְתֶּם בְּמוֺתִי‎ when I die, so ye shall bury me, etc., + often; after conjs., as כִּי‎ Gen 29:15, יַעַן‎ 1Kin 20:28; Isa 3:16f., תַּחַת‎ 60:15, etc., (see Dr§ 123).

b. וַּ ‎ consecutive and the imperfect (but much less frequently than the perfect), as Gen 30:30 the little that thou hadst, וַיִּפְרֹץ‎ it hath increased, Exod 9:21; 2Sam 4:10; 1Kin 9:20f. 15:13 +; after time-determinations, Gen 22:4 on the third day וַיִּשָּׂא‎ then Abraham lifted up his eyes, 19:15; 27:34; 37:18; 1Sam 6:6; 12:8; Isa 6:1; Hosea 11:1 when Israel was a child, וָאֹהֲבֵהוּ‎ then I loved him, +; occasionally after conjunctions, as כַּאֲשֶׁר‎ Exod 16:34, יַעַן‎ 1Sam 15:23, לְמַעַן‎ Isa 45:4, אִם‎ Psa 59:16 (Dr§ 127).

c. in other cases (not 'consecutive') — all more or less uncommon: namely a. וְ‎ closely joined to the imperfect Gen 13:9 if to the left, וְאֵימִינָה‎ then I will take the right (compare 2Sam 12:8) Exod 12:3 on the 10th of the month וְיִקְחוּ‎ then let them take, Num 16:5; Isa 43:4; Hosea 4:6; 10:10; Psa 69:33; Job 15:17; 2Sam 22:41; Prov 23:24 Kt (Dr§ 125); β. separated from the verb, Exod 8:22; Lev 7:16 יֵאָכֵל וְהַנּוֺתָר וּמִמָּחֳרָת‎ and on the morrow, then the remainder shall be eaten, Josh 3:3; 1Kin 8:32; Isa 8:7; 48:7; Job 14:7; 20:18; b 23:12; 25:5; 32:14 +; γ. without a verb, Gen 40:9 וְהִנֵּה בַּחֲלֹמִי‎ in my dream, behold, a vine was before me, 40:16; 2Sam 23:3f.; Prov 10:25, and the extreme cases 2Sam 15:34 thy father's slave, מֵאָז וַאֲנִי‎ I was that of old, — but now עַבְדְּךָ וַאֲנִי‎ well, I will be thine, Isa 34:12 (si vera lectio), Job 4:6b דְּרָכֶיךָ וְתֹם תִּקְוָָֽתְךָ‎ thy confidence — it is the uprightness of thy ways, 36:26 חֵקֶר וְלֹא שָׁנָיו מִסְמַּר‎ Ges. seine Jahre, da ist kein Zählen (compare Dr§ 124-5, 128-9). — With 4, 5 compare the Arabic , Wi. § 366 b, 367 c; ii. § 187; Dr§ 185 end.

צרע.def:
H6879. tsara

[צָרַע‎] verb denominative, only in passive, be struck with leprosy, leprous; —

Qal Participle passive צָרוּעַ אִישׁ‎ Lev 13:44; elsewhere as substantive, = leper, 13:45; 14:3; Num 5:2 (all P), Lev 22:4 (H).

Pu`al Participle מְצֹרָע‎ 2Sam 3:29 +, מְצוֺרָע‎2Chr 26:20; plural מְצֹרָעִים‎ 2Kin 7:3, 8; feminine מְצֹרַ֫עַת‎ Exod 4:6 +, מְצֹרָ֑עַת‎ Num 12:10; — leprous, of hand Exod 4:6 (J), of person Num 12:10 (twice in verse) (E), 2Kin 5:27; 2Chr 26:20; מְצֹרָעִים אֲנָשִׁים‎ 2Kin 7:3; as substantive = leper 2Sam 3:29; 2Kin 5:1, 11; 7:8; 15:5 2Chr 26:21a, 26:21b, 26:23; הַמְּצֹרָע תּוֺרַת‎ Lev 14:2.

צרעה.def:
H6881. Tsorah

צָרְעָה‎ proper name, of a location Σαραα, etc. (compare also LagBN 85), in the Shephelah of Judah (Tel Amarna ‚ar—a, named with Aialuna, Ajalon); — Josh 15:33, but assigned to Dan 19:41; Judg 13:2, 25; 16:31; 18:2, 8, 11; 2Chr 11:10; Neh 11:29; modern ‚ar±a, 15 miles west from Jerusalem, compare GASmGeogr. 218 BuhlGeogr.195.

צרעי.def:
H6882. Tsori

or Tsorathi צָרְעִי‎ see following

צָרְעָתִי‎ adjective, of a people with article as collective noun ׳הַצּ‎ 1Chr 2:53; 4:2 = הַצָּרְעִי‎ 2:54.

צרעת.def:
H6883. tsaraath

צָרַ֫עַת‎35 noun feminine leprosy; — absolute ׳צ‎ Deut 24:3 +, צָרָ֑עַת‎ Lev 13:2 +; construct צָרַ֫עַת‎ 2Kin 5:27 +; suffix צָרַעְתּוֺ‎ 5:3, 6, 7; — leprosy 5:3, 6, 7, 27; 2Chr 26:19; elsewhere only in laws: צ ׳נֶגַע‎ Deut 24:8, and Lev 13:14 (P; 29 t.): הַצ ׳תּוֺרַת‎ 14:57; specific of

a. human disease (as above) צ ׳נֶגַע‎ Lev 13:2 8t.; without ׳נ‎ 13:8 10t.

b. leprosy in a garment Lev 13:47, 49, 51, 52, 59 (צ נֶנַע ׳תּוֺרַת בֶּגֶד‎).

c. in house Lev 14:34 (צ ׳נֶגַע‎), 14:44; house or garment 14:55. — Exact meaning of

b. and

c. dubious, perhaps some fungus or mould; see especially Di Dr-Wh Baen.

צרעתי.def:
H6882. Tsori

or Tsorathi צָרְעִי‎ see following

צָרְעָתִי‎ adjective, of a people with article as collective noun ׳הַצּ‎ 1Chr 2:53; 4:2 = הַצָּרְעִי‎ 2:54.

צרף.def:
H6884. tsaraph

צָרַף‎ verb smelt, refine, test (Late Hebrew id.; Phoenician מצרף‎ smelter; Assyrian ƒurrupu, refined, ƒarpu, silver, naƒraptu, crucible; Arabic is pure, unmixed (especially of wine); **compare pure silver, etc., SchulthGGA, 1902, 673; also ZimGGA, 1899, 250; KAT 3, 650 (Hebrew, etc., borrowed from Assyrian); very doubtful is Sabean צרף‎ silver, money, compare MordtmHim. Inschr. pp. 14, 29 CISiv, No. 291, 1.1); —

Qal Perfect3masculine singular ׳צ‎ Jer 6:29, suffix צְרָפָ֑תְהוּ‎ Psa 105:19; 2masculine singular suffix צְרַפְתָּנִי‎ 17:3, etc.; Imperfect1singular אֶצְרֹף‎ Isa 1:25, suffix אֶצְרְפֶנּוּ‎ Judg 7:4; Imperative masculine singular צרופה‎ Psa 26:2 Kt, צָרְפָה‎ Qr; Infinitive absolute צָרוֺף‎ Jer 6:29; construct לִצְרוֺף‎ Dan 11:35, etc.; Participle active suffix צוֺרְכָּם‎ Jer 9:6, etc.; pass. צָרוּף‎ Psa 12:7, etc.; —

1 smelt, refine: Jer 6:29 (twice in verse) in vain hath he smelted continually (infinitive absolute; figurative of purifying people); so smelt away Isa 1:25 (accusative of dross; figurative); of silver Zech 13:9; Psa 66:10, בַּעֲלִיל צָרוּף כֶּסֶף‎ 12:7 (all simile); of י ׳אִמְרַת‎ 18:31 = 2Sam 22:31; Psa 119:140; Prov 30:5 (אֱלוֺהַּ אִמְרַת‎); refine (men, by trials) Dan 11:35 (+ לַלְבֵּן לִבָרֵר,‎).

2 test Judg 7:4 I will test them (the warriors) for thee (׳י‎ subject); — perhaps also 7:3 (see I. צפר‎); more Generally, of ׳י‎'s testing, trying (the hearts of) men (often || בָּחַן‎) Jer 9:6; Isa 48:10; Zech 13:9; Psa 26:2; 66:10.

3 test (and prove true) a man (subject ׳י‎s saying) Psa 105:19.

4 Participle active as

noun smelter, refiner, hence = goldsmith Judg 17:4; Jer 10:9, 14; 51:17; Isa 40:19 (twice in verse) (but perhaps strike out vb, compare Du Che Marti), 41:7; 46:6; Prov 25:4; as a guild Neh 3:8, 32.

Niph`al Imperfect3masculine plural יִצָּֽרְפוּ‎ Dan 12:10 many shall be refined (by suffering; + יִתְלַבְּנוּ יִתְבָּֽרְרוּ,‎).

Pi`el Participle מְצָרֵף‎ as

noun a refiner, מ ׳כְּאֵשׁ‎ Mal 3:2 (simile of ׳י‎), compare ׳מְ‎ alone 3:3 (+ כֶּסֶף מְטַהֵר‎).

צרפי.def:
H6885. tsorephi

צֹרְפִי‎ noun [masculine] collective goldsmiths; — only ׳בֶּןהַֿצּ‎ Neh 3:31 i.e. belonging to the goldsmiths, a member of their guild.

צרפת.def:
H6886. Tsarephath

צָֽרְפַת‎ proper name, of a location Σαρεπτα: on coast south of Sidon (? smelting-place; on strange form compare LagBN 84; Assyrian ‚ariptu DlPa 284 COT1Kin 17:9; Egyptian Da-ïra-pu-ti WMMAs.u.Eur.184); — ׳צ‎ Obadiah 20; צָֽרְפָ֫תָה‎ 17:9-10, (so Gi; פַ֫תָה‎- van d. H. Baer); modern ‚arfend RobBR ii. 474 ff. PietschmPhön. 58 f..

צרר.def:
H413. el

אֶל‎ (nearly always followed by Makkeph), in poetry אֱלֵי‎ (compare עֲדֵי עֲלֵי,‎), but only in Job ( 1 Samuel 3:22; 1 Samuel 5:26; 1Sam 15:22; 1 Samuel 29:19), with suffix אֵלַיִךְ אֵלֶיךָ, אֵלַי,‎, etc. אֲלֵיכֶם אֵלֵינוּ,‎ & (5 t.) אֲלֵיהֶם אֲלֵכֶם,‎ & אֲלֵהֶם‎ (both very often); once אֵלֵימוֺ‎ Psa 2:5, אֲלֵיהֶן‎, once אֲלֵהֶן‎ Exod 1:19 (Assyrian ilî, Arabic ),

preposition denoting motion to or direction towards (whether physical or mental).

1 of motion to or unto a person or place Gen 2:19, 22; 3:19; 8:9; 14:22; 16:9 etc., after every kind of verb expressing motion (יָצָא הָלַךְ, בּוֺא,‎ etc.) So with נָתַן‎ to give (though ל‎ is here more common) 21:14; 35:4; Deut 13:2 +; מָכַר‎ to sell Deut 37:36, etc. Metaph. Jer 2:19 אֵלַיִךְ פַחְדָּתִי וְלֹא‎ and that my fear (cometh) not unto thee (compare Job 31:23). — Peculiarly Gen 6:16 אַמָּה אֶל‎ unto the length of a cubit, etc. And metaphor in the phrase אֶלֿ(אֱלֵיֿ)גִּיל‎ unto exultation Hosea 9:11; Job 3:22. Once, exceptionally (si vera 1.) = even: 5:5 יִקָּחֵהוּ וְאֶלמִֿצִּגִּים‎ and even out of thorns he taketh it. Sometimes pregnant, as Isa 66:17; Jer 41:7 אֶל זָנָה‎ commit whoredom (by going) to Num 25:1; Ezek 16:26, 28, 29; אֶל דָּרֵשׁ‎ seek (by resorting) to one (that is, for oracles) Deut 18:11; Isa 8:19; 11:10 +; אֶל חָבַר‎ join together (& come) unto Gen 14:3; אֶל הִשְׁכִּים‎ rise early (and go) to 19:27; 24:11 אֶל הִבְרִיח‎ made to kneel down at; 47:18 אֶל תַּם‎ i.e. has been made over to; אֶל מָּחַד‎ to come in fear to Hosea 3:5; Micah 7:17. Opposite is מִן‎, as אֶלהַֿקָּצֶה מִןהַֿקָּצֶה‎ from end to end Exod 26:28; אֶלמֶּֿה מִמֶּה‎ Ezra 9:11 (synonym 2Kin 21:16 לָפֶה מֶּה‎). And of time (rare) אֶלעֵֿת מֵעֵת‎ 1Chr 9:25; אֶליֿוֺם מִיּוֺם‎ Num 30:15 (P) 1Chr 16:23 (in the || Psa 96:2 לְיוֺם מִיּוֺם‎).

2 Where the limit is actually entered, into, Gen 6:18 and thou shalt enter into the ark 7:1; 19:3; 41:21; 42:17; & so after verbs of throwing, casting, putting 37:22 (הִשְׁלִיךְ‎) 39:20 הַסֹּהַר אֶלבֵּֿית וַיִּתְּנֵהוּ‎ put him into the prison house, Exod 28:30 (Lev 8:8) Deut 23:25; so after קָבַר‎ to bury Gen 23:19; 25:9; 49:29; שָׂחַט‎ to squeeze 40:11; מָחָה‎ to blot out Num 5:23, etc.; metaphor Gen 6:6 was pained into or unto his heart, הֵשִׁיב אֶללֵֿב, שָׂם‎ to place, bring. into ( = lay to) heart Deut 4:39; 2Sam 19:20 and elsewhere In connection with a number or multitude into which something enters, in among: 1Sam 10:22 behold he had hid himself אֶלהַֿכֵּלִים‎ in among the baggage, Jer 4:3 sow not אֶלקֹֿצִים‎ in among thorns.

3 Of direction towards anything: (a) of physical acts or states, as Gen 30:40 אֶל הַצּאֹן מְּנֵי נָתַן‎, 39:7 אֶל עֵינָיו נָשָׂא‎, Exod 25:20; Num 6:26, אֶל פָנָיו נָשָׂא‎ (2Kin 9:32 differently), 24:1 אֶל מָּנָיו שָׁת‎, Josh 8:18; Psa 28:2; 1Kin 8:29-30, (to pray towards) 8:38; pregnantly אֶל חָרֵד‎ to tremble (turning) to Gen 42:28, אֶל תָּמַהּ‎ to, wonder (turning) towards 43:33; Isa 13:8, אֶל מָּחַד‎ Jer 36:16: without a verb אֶלמָּֿנִים מָּנִים‎ face to face Gen 32:31 +; אֶלמֶּֿה מֶּה‎ Num 12:8; אֵלַי כִּיאֵֿינֶנּוּ‎ Gen 31:5 the face of Laban, that he is not toward me; י ׳עֵינֵי ׳אֶלפֿ‎ the eyes of ׳י‎ are towards . . . Psa 34:16 (compare 33:18). (b) with words such as אָמַר‎to say to Gen 3:1 + often, דִּבֶּר‎ 8:15 + often, קָרָא‎ 19:5, הִחְמַּלֵּל‎ 20:17 etc., שָׁמַע‎ to hearken to 16:11, הִלֵּל‎ to praise to 12:15 (compare Ezek 13:19 אֶל חִלֵּל‎ to profane to), הִזְכִּיר‎ 40:14. (c) with words expressing the direction of the mind, as קִוָּה‎ to wait Psa 27:14 +; יִחַל‎ to hope Isa 51:5; אֶל נֶפֶשׁ נָשָׂא‎ to lift up the soul (i.e. set the desire) towards Deut 24:15; Psa 25:1; שָׁת אֶל, לֵב שָׂם‎ to set the heart (mind) to Exod 9:21 and elsewhere; אֶל לָמַד‎ to accustom oneself to Jer 10:2; אֶל חָרֵד‎ to shew fear towards 2Kin 4:13; Gen 43:30; Deut 28:32 and thy eyes אֲלֵיהֶם כָּלוֺת‎ failing (with longing) towards them, Lam 4:17; Isa 63:15; 2Sam 3:8; 1Kin 14:13; Psa 40:6; alone, as predicate, directed or disposed towards, Gen 3:16; 4:7; 2Kin 6:11 who of ours is towards (i.e. favours) the king of Syria? Hosea 3:3 אֵלָֽיִח׃ וְגַםאֲֿנִי‎ Ezek 36:9; Hag 2:17; Jer 15:1 (אֶל נַפְשִׁי אֵין‎).

4 Where the motion or direction implied appears from the context to be of a hostile character, אֶל‎ = against: Gen 4:8 ק ׳וַיָּקָם אֶלהֶֿבֶל‎and Cain rose up against Abel (so 1Sam 24:8) 22:12; Exod 14:5; Num 32:14; with נִקְבַּץ‎ Josh 10:6, הָלַךְ‎ Judg 1:10; 20:30; with בָּא‎ of calamity, etc., coming to or upon any one Gen 42:21; Judg 9:57; 1Sam 2:34; 1Kin 14:10 +; Isa 2:4; 3:8 their tongue and doings are ׳אֶליֿ‎ 32:6 (אֶל לְדַבֵּר‎) Hosea 7:15 (compare Nahum 1:9) Hosea 12:5 אֶלמַֿלְאָךְ וַיָּשַׂר‎ and he strove against the angel. Here also belongs in particular the phrase ֗֗֗ אֶל הִנְנִי‎ Behold I am against (thee, you, etc.) Nahum 2:14; Nahum 3:5; Jer 21:13 (23:30-32 על‎) 50:31; 51:25; Ezek 13:8, 20; 21:8; 29:10; 30:22; 34:10; 35:3; 38:3; 39:1 (5:8; 26:3; 28:22; 29:3 על‎: on 36:9 see above)

5 Unto sometimes acquires from the context the sense of in addition to, as Lev 18:18 thou shalt not take אֲחוֺתָהּ אֶל אִשָּׁה‎ a woman to, in addition to, her sister, Josh 13:22 (|| Num 31:8 על‎); 1Sam 14:34 at eat אֶלהַֿחָם‎ together with the blood (14:32 & Generally עַל‎); 1Kin 10:7 אֶל הוֺסִיף‎ (generally עַל‎); Jer 25:26; Ezek 7:26 שְׁמוּעָה אֶל שְׁמוּעָה‎ || (עלׅ‎; 44:7; Lam 3:41 let us lift up אֶלכַּֿמָּ֑יִם לְבָבֵנוּ‎ our hearts together with the hands (compare , Qor 4:2; WAG ii. § 51 c).

6 Metaphor in regard to, concerning, on account of : thus הִתְאַבֵּל‎ to mourn concerning 1Sam 15:35; הִנָּחֵם‎ to repent as regards 2Sam 24:16; דָּרַשׁ‎ to inquire 1Kin 14:5 הִתְמַּלֵּל‎ to pray with regard to 1Sam 1:27; 2Kin 19:20; צָעַק‎ to cry 8:3 (8:5 על‎); נֶעֳצַב‎ be pained 1Sam 20:34; נִחַם‎ to comfort 2Sam 10:2; more Generally 1Kin 16:13; 21:22; אֶלנֶֿפֶשׁ‎ on account of, for the sake of, one's life 19:3; 2Kin 7:7 (Gen 19:17 על‎). (עַל‎ is more common in this sense.) And specially with verbs of saying, narrating, telling, etc. with regard to, as אָמַר‎ 20:2; Isa 29:22; 37:21, 33 +; דִּבֶּר‎ 2Sam 7:19; Jer 40:16 b; סִמֵּר‎ Psa 2:7; 69:27; צִוָּה‎ Isa 23:11; שָׁמַע‎ Ezek 19:4; אֶל הַשְּׁמוּעָה‎ the report regarding. . . 1Sam 4:19. (Not frequently, ext. in the case of אָמַר‎.)

7 Of rule or standard, according to (rare): ֗֗֗ אֶלמִּֿי‎ according to the command of, Josh 15:13; 17:4; 21:3 (generally עַלמִּֿי‎); אֶלנָֿבוֺן‎ according to what is fixed = of a certainty 1Sam 23:23; 26:4 (see Dr): perhaps Psa 5:1; 80:1 (45:1 עַל‎).

8 Expressing presence at a spot, against; at, by, not merely after verbs expressing or implying motion (compare 1, Gen 24:11), as Josh 11:5 and they came and encamped together מֵרוֺם אֶלמֵֿי‎ at the waters of Merom, 1Sam 5:4 cut off (and fallen) on to the threshold, 2Sam 2:23 and elsewhere and smote him אֶלהַֿחֹמֶשׁ‎ in or on the belly, Deut 33:28; Exod 29:12; Lev 4:7; but also in other cases, as Josh 5:3 and he circumcised the Israelites אֶל‎ against, at the hill of the foreskins, 22:11 have built an altar הַיַּרְדֵּן גְּלִילוֺת אֶל‎ by the districts of Jordan, Judg 12:6; 2Sam 3:32, 14:30 & 18:4 אֶליַֿד‎ at the side of (elsewhere יַד עַל לְיַד,‎), 1Kin 13:20 as they were sitting אֶלהַֿשֻּׁלְחָן‎ at the table, 2Kin 11:14 אֶלהַֿמֶּלֶךְ‎ by the king, Jer 41:12 and found him by the great waters, etc., 46:10 מְּרָת אֶלנְֿהַר‎ by the Euphrates, Ezek 3:15; 11:11; 17:8; 31:7; 40:18; 43:3; 47:7; 48:12.

9 Prefixed to other preps. it combines with them the idea of motion or direction to: thus אֶלאַֿחֲרֵי‎ 2Sam 5:23; 2Kin 9:18-19, אֶלאַֿחֲרַי סֹב‎ turn to behind me, Zech 6:5 (where אֶל‎ is pleonastic, probably due to clerical error; note אל יצא‎ before & after); אֶלבֵּֿין‎ in between Ezek 31:10, 14; אֵלבֵּֿינוֺת‎ similarly 10:2; לְ ׳אֶלמִֿבֵּית‎ to (the part) within (see below בַּיִת‎), in within Lev 16:15; 2Kin 11:15 || have her forth in within the ranks; אֶלמֿוּל‎ see מוּל‎; לְ ׳אֶלמִֿנֶּגֶב‎ unto the south of Josh 15:3; לְ ׳אֶלמִֿחוּץ‎ to the outside of Lev 4:12, 21 +; אֶלנֹֿכַח‎ to the front of Num 19:4; אֶלתַּֿחַת‎ Judg 6:19; 1Kin 8:6 and elsewhere (see below תַּחַת‎).

Note I. — In Gen 20:13 וג אִמְרִילִֿי ׳שָׁמָּה נָבוֺא אֲשֶׁר אֶלכָּֿלהַֿמָּקוֺם‎; Num 33:54 וג ׳אֶלאֲֿשֶׁר‎; Prov 17:8 (compare Deut 16:6); — אֶל‎ appears to be used by a species of attraction; the idea of motion involved in the relative clause influencing illogically the beginning of the sentence and causing אֶל‎ to be used instead of בְּ‎. In 31:14 אֵלֵיהֶם‎, as pointed, can only be from אַיִל‎ III or IV (q. v.); if the word be taken as the Pronoun with suffix (Hi Ke), אֲלֵיהֶם‎ must be read.

Note 2. — There is a tendency in Hebrew, especially manifest in Samuel Kings Jeremiah Ezekiel, to use אֶל‎ in the sense of עַל‎; sometimes אֶל‎ being used exceptionally in a phrase or construction which regularly, and in accusative with analogy, has עַל‎; sometimes, the two prepositions interchanging, apparently without discrimination, in the same or parallel sentences. Thus (a) Josh 5:14 אֶלמָּֿנָיו וִיִּמֹּל‎; 1Sam 13:13 י ׳הֵקִים אֶליִֿשְׂרָאֵל אֶתמַֿמְלַכְתְּךָ‎; 14:34 (see below 5); 17:3 אֶלהָֿהָר עֹמְדִים‎ (contractee עַל‎ Deut 11:29); 19:16; 2Sam 6:3; 20:23 (contracted 8:16) 1Kin 13:29; 18:46 (contracted 2Kin 3:15 על‎) Jer 35:15; Ezek 7:18. (b) Judg 6:37 and upon (עַל‎) all the earth let there be dryness, 6:39 let there be dryness on (אֶל‎) the fleece; 1Sam 14:10 come up עָלֵינוּ‎, 14:12 come up אֵלֵינוּ‎; 16:23 & 16; 16:13 & 18:10 אֶל צָלַח‎, 10:6 and elsewhere עַל צָלַח‎; 25:17 evil is determined כָּלבֵּֿיתוֺ וְעַל אֶלאֲֿדֹנֵינוּ‎; 25:25; 27:10; 2Sam 2:9 וְ֗֗֗עַל וְ֗֗֗עַל וְ֗֗֗עַל וְ֗֗֗אֶל וְ֗֗֗אֶל אֶל וַיַּמְלִכֵהוּ‎; 3:29 ֗֗֗ וְאֶל ֗֗֗ עַל יָחֻלוּ‎ 2Kin 8:3 & 5; 9:6 & 3; Jer 19:15; 25:2; 26:15 ye lay innocent blood הַזּאֹת וְאֶלהָֿעִיר עֲלֵיכֶם‎; 27:19; 28:8; 33:14; 34:7; 36:31; 37:13-14, Ezek 18:6, 11 & 15; 21:12 etc. Psa 79:6 (Jer 10:25 על‎ twice). It is probably that this interchange, at least in many cases, is not original, but due to transcribers.

Conversely, though not with the same frequency, עַל‎ occurs where analogy would lead us to expect אֶל‎, or even in juxtaposition with אֶל‎, as 1Sam 1:10 עַל הִתְמַּלֵּל‎ to pray to (1:26 אֶל‎); 1:13; 25:25 אֶלעַ֗֗֗ל‎; 1Kin 20:43 עַלבֵּֿיתוֺ וַיֵּלֶךְ‎ (21:4 אֶל‎); Isa 22:15; Jer 11:2; 23:35; 31:12. compare DrSm i. 13, 13; ii. 8, 7; 15, 4.

צררה.def:
H6888. Tsererah

[צְרֵרָה‎] proper name, of a location צְרֵרָ֫תָה‎ Judg 7:22 (Γαραγαθα, ᵐ5‎. of L καὶ ἦν συνηγμένη), usually thought corrupt for צְרֵדָ֫תָה‎, and in nay case probably = צָֽרְתָן‎, q. v. (GFM).

צרת.def:
H6889. Tsereth

צֶ֫רֶת‎ proper name, masculine in Judah 1Chr 4:7, Αρεθ, ᵐ5‎ of L Σαρηθ.

צרת השחר.def:
H6890. Tsereth

Hashshachar הַשַּׁ֫חַר צֶרֶת‎ proper name, of a location assigned to Reuben Josh 13:19, Σεραδα και Σειων, ᵐ5‎ of L Σαρθ; compare modern eƒ-Sara, on spur of Mt. 'A‰‰ârûs, east of Dead Sea BuhlGeogr. 268.

צרתן.def:
H6891. Tsarethan

צָֽרְתָן‎ proper name, of a location in Jordan valley, near ford, BuhlGeogr. 181; exact site known; Josh 3:16 (Καθιαιρειν, ᵐ5‎ of L Καριαθιαρειμ), 1Kin 7:46 (Σειρα, ᵐ5‎ of L Σαρθαν) = צְרֵדָ֫תָה‎2Chr 4:17 (Αναμε [i.e. ἀνὰ μέσον] σιρδαθαι; Σα(ρι)δαθα; is Chronicles right?); צָֽרְחַ֫נָה‎ 1Kin 4:12 (Σεσαθαν, ᵐ5‎ of L Σαρθαν) — compare צְרֵרָתָה‎ Judg 7:22, apparently same place; identity with צְרֵדָה‎ 1Kin 11:26 is usually assumed, but not proven.
